mcaquests.voice.cooldown.brusque: You have already had that out of me. Come back when there is work again.
mcaquests.voice.cooldown.bright: You have done that one! Give it a few days and I will have something new.
mcaquests.voice.cooldown.gentle: You helped with that not long ago. I could not ask again so soon.
mcaquests.voice.cooldown.wry: Asking twice for the same favour would make me a poor host. Later, then.
mcaquests.voice.cooldown.weary: That is done, and I have not thought of anything since. Come back another day.
mcaquests.voice.cooldown.fallback: You did that for me recently. Ask again in a few days.
mcaquests.voice.locked.brusque: There is work I would hand to someone I knew better. Not yet.
mcaquests.voice.locked.bright: I have something bigger in mind for you. Not quite yet, though!
mcaquests.voice.locked.gentle: There is something, but I am not ready to ask it of you. Not today.
mcaquests.voice.locked.wry: I do have a thing that wants doing. Its moment has not come round.
mcaquests.voice.locked.weary: There is a job waiting. It is not waiting on me.
mcaquests.voice.locked.fallback: There is something I would ask of you, but not yet.
mcaquests.voice.no_quests.brusque: Nothing needs doing. Do not stand about on my account.
mcaquests.voice.no_quests.bright: All caught up here! Come and find me again soon.
mcaquests.voice.no_quests.gentle: I am all right for now. Thank you for asking, though.
mcaquests.voice.no_quests.wry: The rarest thing in this village: a day with nothing to mend.
mcaquests.voice.no_quests.weary: Nothing. Ask me again when the season turns.
mcaquests.voice.no_quests.fallback: I do not need anything right now.
mcaquests.voice.greeting.brusque: You again. Well. Since you are here.
mcaquests.voice.greeting.bright: There you are! I was hoping someone would come by.
mcaquests.voice.greeting.gentle: Oh - hello. I did have something, if you have a moment.
mcaquests.voice.greeting.wry: You have the look of someone with a free afternoon.
mcaquests.voice.greeting.weary: If you are offering, I will not say no.
mcaquests.voice.greeting.fallback: There is something you could help with.

mcaquests.project.guardhouse_stockpile.a: The watch is short on steel and arrows. Bring what you can and we'll arm the guardhouse.
Every ingot and arrow helps. Keep them coming.
mcaquests.project.guardhouse_stockpile.f: Now we shore up the walls. Stone, and plenty of it.
The masons are waiting on that stone.
mcaquests.project.library_restoration.ga: Our shelves are bare. Paper and books would let us begin the restoration.
mcaquests.project.library_restoration.ca: Now we need every librarian's hand to catalogue what we've recovered.
Speak with the other librarians to finish the catalogue.
mcaquests.project.festival_preparation.g: A festival needs a feast! Bring bread and cooked meat for the tables.
The feast tables are still half empty.
mcaquests.project.festival_preparation.d: Light the square — torches everywhere for the celebration!
A few more lights and the square will be ready.
mcaquests.project.festival_preparation.c: Everything is ready. Let the festival begin!
mcaquests.project.well_repair.title: Repair the Village Well
mcaquests.project.well_repair.gather_sto: The well has crumbled. Bring stone and we'll start the repairs.
We need more stone before we can rebuild.
mcaquests.project.well_repair.rebuild.of: Now lay the bricks and the well will flow again.
mcaquests.project.well_repair.rebuild.in: Set the stone bricks around the well.
mcaquests.project.after_raid_recovery.cl: The raid left monsters lurking. Clear them out so we can rebuild in peace.
There are still threats near the walls.
mcaquests.project.after_raid_recovery.re: With the danger past, we need timber and food to rebuild.
mcaquests.project.missing_villager_searc: One of our neighbours hasn't come home. Ask three different mapmakers here in the village whether they've seen anything.
Keep asking around the village — some mapmaker must know something.
If they're out there, they'll need food and light. Gather supplies for the search party.
The search party still needs supplies.
mcaquests.quest.farmer_wheat_request.off: The fields have been kind, but I am short on wheat for the next batch of bread. Could you bring me 24 wheat?
mcaquests.quest.farmer_wheat_request.acc: Thank you. Bring it back when you can, and I will make it worth your time.
mcaquests.quest.farmer_wheat_request.rea: That wheat will help more than you know. Shall we settle up?
mcaquests.quest.farmer_wheat_request.com: You kept your word. I will remember that.
mcaquests.quest.guard_clear_the_night.of: The dead have been restless near the walls. Put down five zombies and the village will sleep easier.
mcaquests.quest.guard_clear_the_night.ac: Good. Watch your back out there.
mcaquests.quest.guard_clear_the_night.de: Then keep your blade close. They will not wait.
mcaquests.quest.guard_clear_the_night.in: How many of them are left standing?
mcaquests.quest.guard_clear_the_night.re: Five down? The watch owes you a debt.
mcaquests.quest.guard_clear_the_night.co: The village is safer for your work tonight.
mcaquests.quest.cartographer_scout_the_l: My maps grow stale. Travel to a nearby forest and bring back what you see.
Wonderful. Mind the treeline and remember the way.
Have you reached the forest yet?
You found it! Tell me everything.
These notes will fill in the blank corners of my charts.

mcaquests.quest.adventurer_into_the_deep: I've crossed every ridge in this world but never the fire below. Step through a portal and see the Nether for us both.
Ha! A kindred spirit. Bring back a tale worth telling.
Some doors are best left shut. I understand.
Have you braved the portal yet?
You walked the burning lands and returned! Quickly — tell me everything.
Now THAT is an adventure. We'll drink to it. Take this, friend.
mcaquests.quest.adventurer_relic_hunt.di: They say there's a city buried in the deep dark, older than any village. I'm too long in the tooth to reach it — but you? Step inside its walls and tell me it's real.
Tread softly down there. Some things sleep, and ought to keep sleeping.
Wise, perhaps. The deep dark keeps what it takes.
Have you found the ancient city yet? Mind the dark — and the silence.
You stood inside it? Truly? Tell me everything.
An ancient city, walked and survived. You've done what I only ever dreamed. Take this — you've more than earned it.
mcaquests.quest.adventurer_trailblazer.d: They say you can see the whole world from the high peaks. Climb the mountains and let me live it through your eyes.
Pack warm and tread careful. The heights are no joke.
The summit waits for braver boots, then.
Have you reached the high country yet?
You stood above the clouds! I can see it in your eyes. Magnificent.
One day I'll make that climb myself. Until then — well earned.
mcaquests.quest.archer_cull_from_afar.di: A pack of skeletons rattles around the old field, and I'll not waste good arrows on a clumsy shot. Drop eight of them — show me a marksman's work.
Loose clean and let none get within a sword's reach.
Then I'll thin them myself, slow as that'll be.
How many of the bone-rattlers have you dropped?
Eight clean kills. That is how a bow is meant to sing.
You shoot like you were born with a string in hand. Well done.
mcaquests.quest.archer_fletchings.title: Fletchings
mcaquests.quest.archer_fletchings.dialog: An arrow flies no straighter than its feathers. Bring me 16 and I'll keep my quiver true.
Chase down a few birds for me. I'll wait at the range.
Crooked arrows, crooked shots. A shame.
Sixteen fine feathers — every shaft will sing now.
You keep my aim honest. I won't forget it.
mcaquests.quest.archer_marksman.title: Marksman's Wager
mcaquests.quest.archer_marksman.dialogue: Care for a wager? Drop 6 skeletons at range before they close on you. I say you can't.
Ha! Prove me wrong, then. Aim for the skull.
Wise. They shoot back, after all.
Six clean shots? You've won fair and square. Well shot!
I lost the bet but gained a worthy archer. Take your winnings.
mcaquests.quest.archer_spider_nest.title: Clear the Nest
mcaquests.quest.archer_spider_nest.dialo: A spider nest has spilled out past the treeline and they hunt by night. Loose your arrows and clear out six before they reach the homes.
Pick them off at range. Don't let them close.
Then keep your shutters latched tonight.
How many of the eight-legged horde have you felled?
Six skewered and the rest scattered. Fine archery.
You've a steady draw. The watch could use your bow again.
Cold months mean a hungry forge. Lay in 24 coal and I'll keep every hearth in the village lit.
Good. A warm village is a living village.
Two dozen lumps — that'll see us to spring.
You've kept the cold from a lot of doors today.
mcaquests.quest.armorer_copper_plating.d: I'm trying a new trim — copper takes a lovely shine. Sixteen ingots and I'll plate a parade set.
It'll green with age, but oh, the gleam at first! Thank you.
Plain steel for the parade, then. Dull.
Sixteen bright ingots! The captain's armor will dazzle.
A craftsman appreciates good materials. As do I, you.
mcaquests.quest.armorer_forge_ahead.dial: The militia needs shields and my hands are full. Craft 2 of them and I'll pay for the labour.
Plank and iron — you know the pattern. Good.
The recruits will have to duck, then.
Two sturdy shields. The watch will stand a little safer.
Fine craftsmanship. There's a place for you at this anvil.
mcaquests.quest.armorer_iron_for_the_for: The forge is hungry and my stores are low. Six iron ingots and I'll keep the village armored.
Good steel starts with good iron. Off you go.
Six ingots of honest iron. Now we can work.
Next plate I beat is yours at a fair price.
mcaquests.quest.butcher_fresh_cuts.title: Fresh Cuts
mcaquests.quest.butcher_fresh_cuts.dialo: My block's been bare all week. Round up 12 raw beef and I'll have something to carve.
Mind the horns. Cattle don't give up easy.
Got any beef for the block?
Twelve good cuts! Now that's a butcher's morning.
You keep the village fed. I won't forget it.
mcaquests.quest.butcher_hearty_meal.dial: Hungry mouths at the inn tonight. Bring me 6 cooked steaks and no one goes to bed empty.
Good. A full belly keeps a village content.
Six steaks, well cooked. The pot's saved tonight.
There's always a plate here for you.
mcaquests.quest.butcher_poultry_run.dial: Chicken's on the menu tonight. Six cooked birds and the inn won't go hungry.
Six golden birds. The cook will be thrilled.
mcaquests.quest.butcher_smoked_supply.di: The smokehouse is empty and market day's coming. Bring me 8 cooked porkchops and I'll stock the stall.
Good. Folk pay well for a proper roast.
Empty hooks make for a poor butcher.
Any pork for the smokehouse yet?
Eight fine chops! The stall will sell out by noon.
You've a knack for this. Come back any time.
mcaquests.quest.cartographer_edge_of_the: Every map I draw ends at the same void. Reach the End itself and tell me what lies past the edge.
No cartographer has charted it and returned. Be the first.
The blank space at the world's rim will have to wait.
Have you found the way to the End?
You stood at the edge of everything! Quickly — before you forget the shape of it.
This map will bear your name at its farthest corner. Legendary.
mcaquests.quest.cartographer_guide_the_s: I've sketches enough to fill a book, but it's dark and my drafting table is across rough ground. Keep me safe and I'll lead us back to it before my notes blow away.
Splendid. Mind the path while I mind the maps.
Then I'll clutch my papers and risk it alone.
The table's this way — keep the dark off my back.
My drafting table! Now the real work begins.
Every line I draw tonight, I owe to you. My thanks, escort.
mcaquests.quest.cartographer_high_ground: I can't map what I can't see. Climb to the mountains and take in the lay of the land for me.
From a peak you can see for leagues. Go carefully on the climb.
The highlands stay a blank on my map, then.
Have you reached the peaks yet?
You've stood on the roof of the world! Tell me what you saw.
The mountains are charted at last. Wonderful work.
mcaquests.quest.cartographer_spare_parch: A map eats paper like nothing else. Twelve sheets and I can chart the next valley.
Excellent. The blank spaces won't fill themselves.
The edges of the map stay a mystery, then.
Have you found me any paper?
Twelve sheets — enough for a proper survey. My thanks.
I'll mark something useful for you on the next map.
mcaquests.quest.aging_parent_1_warm_meal: My parent grows older and frailer by the season, and I can't always be there. Would you carry six loaves to them and see they eat a proper warm meal? It would ease my heart.
Thank you. You'll find them near home — they don't wander far these days.
I understand. I'll try to get away myself, somehow.
Has my parent had a proper meal yet?
They ate well? Oh, that's a weight off my shoulders.
Knowing someone looked in on them means more than I can say. Come back — there's more I'd ask of a friend like you.
mcaquests.quest.aging_parent_2_remedy.di: My parent's taken ill and my own remedies aren't helping. A golden carrot, pressed into their hand by someone who cares — would you tend to them for me? I can't bear to see them suffer.
Bless you. Be gentle — they're prouder than they are strong, these days.
Please reconsider. They haven't many seasons left to waste on stubbornness.
Have you tended my parent yet? How do they fare?
The color's back in their cheeks? Oh, thank the light.
You gave my parent ease when I couldn't. There's one last thing I'd ask — but it can wait until they've rested.
mcaquests.quest.aging_parent_3_last_walk: My parent wishes to walk the old path one more time before their strength fails for good — but they shouldn't go alone. Guard them as they lead the way, and see them safely back to their bed. It would mean the world to us both.
Walk slow, and let them set the pace. Let them have this.
Please — they may not get another chance to ask.
Are they alright out there? Keep close to them, won't you?
Back home and resting easy? Then they had their walk after all.
You gave my parent one last good day, and gave me peace to carry forever. There's no kindness greater than that. Thank you — from the bottom of my heart.
mcaquests.quest.courting_1_first_gift.di: You've been on my mind more than I'd like to admit. I'd not turn away a handful of poppies from someone like you — three would do, if you're so inclined.
Oh! Well. I'll be waiting, then. Don't keep me too long.
Of course. Forget I said anything.
Still gathering those poppies, are you?
Poppies, for me? They're beautiful. You shouldn't have — but I'm glad you did.
I'll press one of these in a book to remember today. Come find me again, won't you?
mcaquests.quest.courting_2_walk_together: It's a fine evening for a walk, and I'd feel safer — happier — with you beside me. Let me lead us out to the next village and back. Keep the dark off us and I'll keep the company sweet.
Then give me your arm and let's not hurry.
Another evening, maybe. I'll hold you to it.
Stay close — the stars are better shared.
What a walk that was. I didn't want it to end.
I'll remember this evening a long while. You make the whole world feel safer.
mcaquests.quest.courting_3_meet_the_fami: Things are... serious now, aren't they? Then it's time you met my family properly. Take a cake and put it in their hands yourself — make a good impression, and so will I.
Don't be nervous. They'll adore you. Probably.
...You're not having second thoughts, are you?
Have you found them yet? They're expecting you — cake in hand, mind.
A whole cake! Oh, they'll be charmed before you say a word.
They loved you — I knew they would. It feels right, you and me. It really does.
My heart's quite made up about you. There's only one thing left to ask — but a promise like that deserves a ring. Bring me four gold, and let me have it shaped into something forever.
Four gold, and then... well. You know what then. Hurry back to me.
Take your time. Some things shouldn't be rushed. I'll wait.
Have you the gold yet? My hands won't stop fidgeting.
Gold enough for a ring — and for a promise. You know what I'm asking, don't you?
Then it's settled, here and now: it's you, and only you. Whatever comes, we face it together.
mcaquests.quest.farmer_family_1_wheat.di: You have a kind face. My harvest came up short this year — could you spare me 16 wheat to see us through?
Thank you. A full granary makes for an easy winter.
No matter. The fields will keep.
You've a friend in this family now. Come back soon; there's always more to do.
mcaquests.quest.farmer_family_2_expand.d: With your help we ate well — now I want to break new ground. Bring me 12 bone meal and I'll double the field.
New rows by spring! I can already picture it.
The old field will have to do for now.
Any bone meal yet? The soil's hungry.
That'll green the whole hillside. Splendid!
Twice the harvest next year, thanks to you.
mcaquests.quest.farmer_family_3_apprenti: My own youngest works the far field through lunch and forgets to eat. Find them and put 6 bread in their hands before sundown, would you?
Quick now — a hungry helper makes careless cuts.
I'll holler at them myself, then.
Have you found them out there? They'll not come in on their own.
Fed and grinning, I'll wager. Good of you.
They look up to you now, you know. As do I.
Sundown came and went, and the poor thing went hungry. Come round again tomorrow and we'll try once more.
mcaquests.quest.farmer_family_4_feast.di: The harvest is in and we're holding a feast — and you're guest of honour. Carry a cake to my kin and the table's complete.
Wonderful! I'll set you a place by the fire.
The offer stands whenever you're ready, friend.
Have you reached them with the cake? Everyone's gathering.
A cake fit for the whole village — come, sit!
You're family now, plain and simple. Whatever you need, our door is open.
mcaquests.quest.guard_safety_1_clear.dia: The dead crowd our walls each night. Cut down 6 zombies and give the watch a night's rest.
Stay sharp out there. I'll hold the gate.
Then we stand the wall alone, as ever.
How many have you put down?
Six fewer shamblers. The watch thanks you.
You've a steady hand. I could use you again.
mcaquests.quest.guard_safety_2_patrol.di: Spiders have nested past the treeline. Clear out 4 of them before they reach the houses — and be quick about it.
Go now. Daylight won't wait for you.
Then pray they don't come calling tonight.
The treeline's quiet again. Good work.
Reliable as the sunrise, you are. Let's see about the recruits.
Too slow — the nest reached the fences while you dawdled. Catch your breath and we'll try again.
mcaquests.quest.guard_safety_2b_amends.d: The spiders reached the houses while you tarried. No grudges — but make it right: bring me 16 torches to relight the watchtower.
A lit tower is half the battle. Off you go.
Then the tower stays dark, and so does my mood.
The tower's still cold. Those torches?
Light at last. We'll call it square.
Everyone slips once. What matters is you came back. Now — the recruits.
mcaquests.quest.guard_safety_3_militia.d: Folk want to defend themselves but have nothing to drill with. Forge me 2 iron swords for the recruits and we'll make a militia of them.
Good steel makes good soldiers. I'll round them up.
Bare hands it is, then. Foolishness.
Two fine swords — the recruits will be thrilled.
The village can stand on its own now, and that's your doing. You'll always have a place on this wall.
mcaquests.quest.jobless_friendship_1_err: Oh — hello! Nobody asks me for much. My knees ache too badly for the orchard, though. Could you fetch me 6 apples?
Truly? How kind. Sweet ones, if you can.
That's alright. People are busy. I understand.
Did you find any apples, friend?
Six lovely apples! You remembered an old soul.
Sit with me sometime, won't you? It gets quiet out here.
mcaquests.quest.jobless_friendship_2_fav: It's... a strange thing to ask. Someone I loved is buried past the hill. Would you lay 3 poppies there for me? My legs won't carry me that far anymore.
Thank you. Tell them — no, just lay the flowers. They'll know.
Of course. It's too much to ask a near-stranger.
Have you been to the hill yet?
You did it. You actually did it. Bless you.
I haven't trusted anyone with that in years. You're not a stranger anymore.
mcaquests.quest.jobless_friendship_2b_un: You set that favour aside — it's alright, truly. It was a heavy thing to ask. If you'd still like to help, just share a meal with me: 4 sweet berries from the bushes?
Something small. That's all I ever really wanted.
No rush at all, friend. Whenever you can.
Berries! And company. That's plenty for an old heart.
You came back even after setting it down. That means more than the flowers would have.
mcaquests.quest.jobless_friendship_3_fri: I want to do something for YOU for once. Help me bake — bring 8 cookies and we'll have a little party, just the two of us and whoever wanders by.
A party! Oh, it's been an age since I had a reason to smile.
Another day, then. I'll save you a seat regardless.
Are the cookies coming? I dusted off the good plates!
Cookies, friends, and an old fool grinning ear to ear!
You turned my quiet little life around. Take this — it was my dearest friend's, long ago. I'd like you to have it now.
mcaquests.quest.librarian_knowledge_1_in: I'm beginning a chronicle of this village, but my inkwell is dry. Could you bring me 4 ink sacs to start?
The story will keep, I suppose.
Any ink for the chronicle yet?
Fine dark ink — now we may truly begin.
You've a curious mind. Stay a while; there is more to this work.
mcaquests.quest.librarian_knowledge_2_lo: Half my references fell apart with age. Bring me 3 books and I'll rebind the chronicle's sources.
Careful with the spines — old paper is delicate.
Then the gaps in the record remain.
Three sturdy volumes — the references are whole again.
You're as much a part of this chronicle as the ink now.
mcaquests.quest.librarian_knowledge_3_sh: The chronicle is finished, and I want it shared, not shelved. Bring 3 bookshelves and we'll open a reading room for the whole village.
A library the village can call its own — at last!
Knowledge hoarded is knowledge lost. But as you wish.
Are the shelves on their way?
Three shelves — the reading room is ready to open!
Generations will read what we made together. Take this, with my deepest thanks — and my friendship.
mcaquests.quest.lost_child_1_trail.title: Bring Them Home
mcaquests.quest.lost_child_1_trail.dialo: My child is gone — wandered off days ago and never came back. They loved the forest. Please, search the woods for any trace of them. I'm out of my mind with worry.
Bless you. Look where the trees grow thick — that's where they'd go.
Then who will look, if not you? Please, reconsider.
Have you reached the forest? Any sign at all?
You searched the woods? Tell me — tell me you found something.
Footprints, heading deeper. They were alive when they passed here. There's still hope — we have to follow it.
mcaquests.quest.lost_child_2_deeper.dial: The trail leads to the old mineshaft. They must have sheltered down there in the dark — go quickly, before the cold or the creatures find them first, and walk them home yourself. Hurry, I beg you.
Take a torch and don't stop. Every moment matters now.
Don't give up on them — not when we're this close!
Are you in the tunnels yet? And when you have them, don't let them out of your sight on the way back.
You have them. You actually have them. Come here, both of you.
Sheltering in the dark, frightened but whole — you found them. You actually found them. Bless you a thousand times.
mcaquests.quest.lost_child_2b_cold_trail: We were too slow at the mine and the trail went cold... but I won't stop. Light a candle at the shrine for me — three of them — so they can find their way back, wherever they are.
Thank you for not giving up on us. Three candles, for hope.
Even a flicker of light would mean so much right now.
Have you the candles for the shrine?
Three little flames against all that dark. It's something. It's hope.
Maybe they'll see the light and follow it home. Maybe. You kept hope alive when I couldn't — and that's a gift in itself.
Whatever this long search has cost us, I want to mark its end with warmth, not grief. Bring a cake and we'll set a table — a homecoming, in hope or in memory.
Thank you. Come share it with us. You're family now, after all this.
Please — don't let it end on a cold note. Not after everything.
Is the cake coming? The table feels too quiet without it.
A proper cake. Sit with us, won't you? You've earned a place at this table.
Through every dark mile of this, you never once turned away. Whatever the woods took from us, they couldn't take that. We will never forget you.
mcaquests.quest.mapmaker_expedition_1_su: I mean to map the lands past the ridge, but my desk is bare. Bring me 8 paper and we'll begin the first survey.
Wonderful. Every great map starts with a blank page.
No matter — the frontier isn't going anywhere.
Any paper yet? My quills are restless.
Crisp, clean sheets — perfect. Let's get to work.
A fine start. Come back and we'll push past the ridge together.
mcaquests.quest.mapmaker_expedition_2_ex: The light's right for a survey, but it won't last. Bring me a compass and 4 glass panes before dusk and we'll chart the ridge today.
Quick now — shadows lengthen fast out here.
Another clear day will come. Probably.
Daylight's burning — the compass and glass, hurry!
Just in time! Hold the lens steady while I sketch.
We've charted the ridge. The frontier proper is next — and I can't imagine doing it without you.
Dusk beat us, and the survey's spoilt. Don't fret — come by tomorrow and we'll salvage what we can.
mcaquests.quest.mapmaker_expedition_2b_s: The rushed survey smudged, but its bones are sound. Bring me 6 paper and I'll redraw what we lost — take all the time you need this round.
Patience makes a truer map than haste ever did.
The smudge will keep. So will I.
Whenever the paper's ready, friend. No deadline this time.
Fresh sheets — now I can salvage the ridge lines.
Redrawn and better for it. The frontier's still out there waiting — shall we?
mcaquests.quest.mapmaker_expedition_3_fr: Everything's led to this: the frontier itself. Bring me 2 empty maps and we'll set down the first true chart of these lands — together.
Two maps, two cartographers. History, in ink.
The edge of the world can wait one more day.
The frontier's still blank on the page. Those maps?
Spread them out — let's fill in the unknown.
There. The frontier has a face now, and your name belongs on this map as much as mine. Wherever you wander, you'll never be off the chart again.
My faith says there is fire beneath the world. Step through a portal and bear witness for me.
Go with courage. Return with truth.
Perhaps the abyss is best left unseen.
Have you crossed into the fire yet?
You have walked among the flames and lived. Tell me everything.
Your courage humbles me. The temple is in your debt.
The shrine's lanterns have gone dim. Eight glowstone dust would set them alight again.
Light drives back more than shadow. Go safely.
Then the dark endures a little longer.
It shimmers even now. The shrine will glow once more.
May the light you brought return to you tenfold.
mcaquests.quest.cleric_grim_harvest.dial: The rituals call for things best gathered after dark. Bring me 10 rotten flesh — don't ask why.
The dead provide, in their way. Tread carefully.
The night keeps its secrets a while longer.
Have you the flesh I asked for?
Ten pieces, ripe and ready. The work can begin.
You have done the temple a quiet service.
Evening prayers ran long and now the dark presses close. Walk with me and keep the wicked things at bay — I'll lead us home to my own bed.
Blessings upon you. Stay near and fear nothing.
Then I'll trust to faith and a quick step. Go in peace.
Not far now. Keep the shadows from our heels.
My own threshold, thank the light. We're home.
You guarded a humble servant through the dark. That is its own blessing — and here is mine to you.
mcaquests.quest.cleric_tend_the_flock.di: Some of our folk have lost their trade and their spirits. Go speak with 3 of the idle ones — just listen.
Kindness is the only sermon that matters. Off you go.
Loneliness will keep until you have time for it.
Have you sat with the lost souls yet?
Three hearts a little lighter for your visit. Bless you.
You tend souls as well as any cleric. Thank you, truly.
I've taken hurt tending others and my own hands shake too much to mend it. Press a golden carrot on me and let the warmth do its work.
Bless you. A healer needs healing too, sometimes.
Then I'll pray it knits on its own. Go in peace.
The wound still aches, friend. That golden carrot?
Ahh — the pain ebbs already. The light provides.
Mended and grateful. Now I can get back to tending the rest. Bless you.
mcaquests.quest.cleric_urgent_medicine.d: A child in the next house burns with fever and the sickness is spreading fast. Bring me 4 glistering melon slices — quickly, before it takes a turn we can't undo.
Hurry, please. Every minute the fever climbs.
Then I'll do what little I can with what I have. Pray it's enough.
Do you have the medicine? The fever's still rising.
You made it in time — give them here, quickly.
The fever broke before dawn. You saved a life today, and the village won't forget it.
You came too late. The fever crested and the child slipped into a dangerous sleep. There may yet be a way to set this right — come speak with me.
mcaquests.quest.cleric_urgent_medicine_r: The child clings on, weak but breathing. There's still hope — gather 6 sweet berries and a honey bottle for a tonic, and we may pull them back yet. Take whatever time you need; just don't fail them twice.
Thank you. Bring what you can; I'll keep watch over them.
I understand. The guilt is a heavy thing to carry.
How goes the gathering? The tonic can wait a little longer.
Everything I need — let me prepare it at once.
The colour's back in their cheeks. You set right what went wrong, and that takes more strength than never falling at all.
mcaquests.quest.farmer_build_the_hayloft: The hayloft's bare and the beasts are hungry. Stack 8 hay bales up by the barn for me?
Right up against the north wall, if you would.
The cows will grumble, but so be it.
Eight bales, neatly stacked. The herd will eat well.
mcaquests.quest.farmer_root_cellar.title: The Root Cellar
mcaquests.quest.farmer_root_cellar.dialo: Winter's coming and the cellar's half empty. Bring me 16 carrots to put by?
Bless you. A full cellar is a quiet winter.
We'll tighten our belts, I suppose.
Sixteen carrots! The cellar thanks you.
You've earned a warm meal whenever you pass through.
mcaquests.quest.farmer_sow_before_the_ra: Rain's the best time to plant! Quick, gather me 16 seeds while the soil's soft.
Hurry now — a good shower won't wait for slow hands.
The rain will pass and the chance with it.
Got those seeds while it's still wet?
Sixteen seeds, ready for the drills. The fields will thank you.
Planted in the rain, harvested in the sun. That's farming.
mcaquests.quest.fisherman_a_taste_of_the: The chef wants pufferfish for a fancy dish — risky eating, that. Land me 2 without poisoning yourself.
Handle them with care. They puff up for a reason.
Safer choice, honestly. But less coin.
Two puffers, and all your fingers intact! Impressive.
The chef will make something extraordinary. Well earned.
mcaquests.quest.fisherman_fresh_catch.di: The nets came up empty today. Could you bring me 8 cod so the village eats well tonight?
Bless you. The sea owes us all a favor now and then.
Hmph. More for the gulls, then.
Eight fine cod! Hand them over and I'll square up.
You'll always have a place at my table.
mcaquests.quest.fisherman_rain_catch.dia: The salmon run thick while it's raining and vanish the moment it clears. Land me 5 of them — but only while the rain holds. Once it stops, the chance is gone.
Then don't dawdle — cast while the clouds are with you.
Fair enough. Not everyone's mad enough to fish a downpour.
Still raining — still biting. Keep at it!
Five rain-fat salmon. The river was generous today.
Caught while the sky wept — those are the sweetest. My thanks.
The rain's gone and so are the salmon. They'll not run again until the next storm. Ah well — there's always the next.
mcaquests.quest.fisherman_salmon_run.dia: Salmon are running upstream. Cast a line and bring me 5 — there's a knack to it.
Patience and a steady hand. You'll get them.
The river will wait for you.
Five salmon, fresh from the hook. Well done.
You've the makings of an angler yet.
mcaquests.quest.fisherman_storm_catch.di: The fish bite best in the rain, if you've the patience for it. Land me 4 cod while the weather holds.
Aye, get out there before the clouds break.
The rain won't last, and neither will the chance.
Four fat cod, rain-caught and the best kind. Nicely done.
Only a true angler fishes through a storm. My respect.
mcaquests.quest.fletcher_a_fine_bow.dial: A hunter's bow snapped clean in two. Craft a new one and I'll see it gets to him.
Good string, springy wood. You know the way of it.
A fine bow indeed! The hunter eats well this winter.
Craftsmanship like yours is rare. My thanks.
mcaquests.quest.fletcher_feather_light.d: No feathers, no fletching, no arrows. Bring me 10 and the quivers stay full.
Chase down a chicken or two. I'll be waiting.
Ten fine feathers. Now the arrows fly true.
Next bundle of arrows is on me.
mcaquests.quest.fletcher_feathers_for_fi: The watch burns through arrows faster than I can fletch them, and another dark night's coming. Bring me sixteen arrows and I'll see the wall stays stocked.
Good. An archer without arrows is just a fellow holding a stick.
Then the quivers run dry, and the wall with them.
How's that bundle of arrows coming?
Sixteen good shafts — that'll keep the watch loosing till dawn.
The wall's well supplied, thanks to you. Steady hands keep the village standing.
mcaquests.quest.fletcher_full_quiver.dia: The watch is down to their last shafts. Bring me 32 arrows and the walls stay defended.
Straight shafts and sharp heads. The guards will thank you.
How many arrows have you for me?
Two and thirty! Every quiver on the wall is full again.
The watch stands ready, thanks to you.
mcaquests.quest.fletcher_knapping.title: Knapping Day
mcaquests.quest.fletcher_knapping.dialog: No flint, no arrowheads. Dig me up 12 pieces from the gravel by the river?
Good eye for stone, I hope. Off you go.
Found any flint in that gravel?
A dozen sharp flints. The knapping can begin.
You've an arrowsmith's patience. Well done.
mcaquests.quest.guard_carry_word_home.di: I'm posted too far out to leave my watch, but the village must hear what I've seen. Make for the village and carry word back for me — quick as you can.
Good. Keep to cover and don't stop running.
Then the message waits, and so does the danger.
Are you at the village yet? They need to know.
Word delivered? Then we've a chance to be ready.
Fast and faithful. The watch could use a runner like you.
mcaquests.quest.guard_dawn_defense.title: Hold Till Dawn
mcaquests.quest.guard_dawn_defense.dialo: The horde won't last past sunrise, but it'll thin us before then. Put down 6 zombies before first light and we'll all see the morning.
Then go — every one you drop is a wall we don't have to mend.
Suit yourself. I'll mind the gate alone, then.
Dawn's coming. How many have you felled?
Six down and the sky's greying. We held.
Sunrise, and the village still standing. That's your doing, soldier.
The sun's up and the work's half done. They slipped past us in the dark — and folk noticed who wasn't there.
mcaquests.quest.guard_defend_the_captain: The dead are pressing the gate and I can't hold them alone. Stand with me — cut down five of the undead before they overrun us.
Then draw your blade, soldier. Stay near me.
Then stand aside and let those who'll fight do it.
Keep them off me! How many have you felled?
Five down and the line holds. We did it.
You stood your ground when it counted. The watch remembers that.
They broke through while you were elsewhere. We'll be mending walls for a week.
mcaquests.quest.guard_hold_the_gate.dial: They're pressing the gate again tonight. Plant your feet by the wall with me and cut down eight of them — give ground and the whole street is theirs.
Then hold this ground. Not one step back.
Then stand aside for those who'll fight.
Hold the line! How many at the gate have you dropped?
Eight down and the gate still ours. Well held.
You stood your ground when it counted. The watch won't forget it.
mcaquests.quest.guard_last_stand.title: The Last Stand
mcaquests.quest.guard_last_stand.dialogu: They're massing thick and we're too few. Hold the village heart with me and put down a dozen before sunrise — if dawn finds them inside the walls, we've lost.
Then we hold till dawn. Steady now.
Then we sell the square dearly without you.
Dawn's a long way off. Keep cutting them down!
A dozen down and grey light on the wall. We held.
You stood the whole night through. They'll tell this one for years.
Dawn came and they were still among the houses. A black night for us all.
mcaquests.quest.guard_night_watch.title: Night Watch
mcaquests.quest.guard_night_watch.dialog: The dead walk thick tonight. Stand the watch with me — put down 4 zombies before dawn.
Keep your back to the wall and your blade up.
Then bar your door and let the watch handle it.
How many have you dropped tonight?
Four down before sunrise. The village slept safe and never knew.
You'd make a fine soldier of the watch. Well held.
mcaquests.quest.guard_phantom_vigil.dial: Sleepless nights bring winged horrors down on us. Strike three phantoms from the sky before they carry off a sleeper.
Keep your eyes up and your aim true.
Then we duck and pray when they swoop.
Still hearing those shrieks overhead. Three of them.
The sky's quiet again. Good shooting.
Folk can rest without watching the rafters now. My thanks.
mcaquests.quest.guard_post_raid_sweep.di: The main fight's done but stragglers still lurk in the alleys and cellars. Sweep the village and put down six of them before they regroup.
Check the dark corners. That's where they hide.
Then we'll be jumping at shadows all night.
Found any of the stragglers yet?
Six rooted out of the alleys. The streets are clean.
Thorough as always. The village can breathe again. Well swept.
mcaquests.quest.guard_skeleton_patrol.di: Archers of bone are picking at our patrols from the ruins. Put down 5 and the roads grow safer.
Close the distance fast — they're deadly at range. Go.
Then keep to cover when you travel.
How many skeletons still rattle out there?
Five clattering heaps. The patrols can breathe easier.
Steady aim and a steadier nerve. The watch salutes you.
mcaquests.quest.guard_spider_season.dial: Spiders have nested too close to the fields. Clear out 4 of them before someone gets bitten.
Watch the treeline. They drop when you least expect it.
Then keep clear of the tall grass after dark.
Four spiders dealt with? The farmers can breathe easy.
The watch is glad to have you, soldier.
mcaquests.quest.guard_the_creeper_proble: Something keeps cratering the road and the garden walls. Hunt down four creepers before they take a house with them.
Carefully, now — let them get close and you'll share the blast.
Then mind your step near the walls.
Any of those hissing wretches dealt with?
Four fewer holes in my road. Good.
The masons thank you, and so do I. Fine work.
mcaquests.quest.guard_torch_the_dark.dia: Monsters spawn where the light fails. Ring the village edge with torches — a dozen should push the dark back past the wall.
Good thinking. Light denies them the ground.
Then we fight in the dark again tonight.
How many torches up along the wall?
The edge is bright as a hearth. They'll think twice now.
A lit wall is a quiet wall. The watch sleeps easier for your work.
mcaquests.quest.guard_wolf_at_the_door.d: A whole pack of the dead is shambling toward the gate. Thin them out — 8 zombies — before they reach the walls.
Hold the line with me. The village is counting on us.
Then bar your shutters and pray the gate holds.
Is the horde thinning at all?
Eight down at the gate! You fought like a soldier of the watch.
The walls held because you stood at them. Honor to you.
mcaquests.quest.leatherworker_cobblers_a: A child's gone barefoot through the mud all week. Stitch up a pair of leather boots for the poor thing?
Snug and dry, mind. Little feet deserve better.
Sturdy little boots! That child will dance through puddles now.
Kindness stitched into leather. Bless you.
mcaquests.quest.leatherworker_rabbit_run: Rabbit hide makes the softest trim. Catch me 6 pelts from the meadow hares?
Quick little things, mind. You'll earn those pelts.
Six soft pelts! The fine collars practically stitch themselves.
You've a hunter's patience. Much obliged.
mcaquests.quest.leatherworker_the_tanner: A big order came in — saddles, satchels, the lot. I'll need 12 leather to fill it.
Good hide makes good coin. Off you go.
I'll tell them it's delayed, then.
Twelve hides! The tannery will run all night.
A fine haul. There's a cut of the profit in it for you.
mcaquests.quest.leatherworker_tough_hide: My tannery's run dry. Eight leather would let me get back to my craft.
Good hide makes good boots. Off you go.
Bare feet for the village, then.
Have you any leather for me?
Eight good hides. The tannery lives again.
I'll stitch you something fine one of these days.
My inkwell has run dry mid-sentence. Bring me 4 ink sacs from the squid in the bay?
Mind the deep water. Knowledge isn't worth drowning for.
The page stays blank a while longer.
Four sacs of good dark ink — the chronicle resumes!
You've quite literally written yourself into our history.
mcaquests.quest.librarian_paper_trail.di: My records are falling behind for want of paper. Could you bring me 20 sheets?
Wonderful. Knowledge must be written down, or it is lost.
A pity. The blank pages will keep their silence.
Twenty crisp sheets! The archive thanks you.
Come back any time — there is always more to record.
mcaquests.quest.librarian_take_the_censu: My records are out of date. Go and speak with 3 of our farmers and note who's still working the fields.
The ledger will gather dust a while longer.
How many farmers have you counted?
Three accounted for — the census is whole again. Splendid.
Tidy work. The archive thanks you, as do I.
mcaquests.quest.librarian_well_read.dial: I am assembling a small library. Three bound books would be a fine start — could you spare them?
Splendid. A village with books is a village with a future.
Another day, perhaps, when the shelves call to you.
Three volumes! These will be read and re-read for years.
You have my lasting gratitude, friend.
mcaquests.quest.mason_clay_works.title: Clay Works
mcaquests.quest.mason_clay_works.dialogu: The kiln's cold for want of clay. Dig me 16 lumps from the riverbank and we'll fire some brick.
Wet work, but the kiln pays it back in warmth. Thank you.
No clay, no brick, no business.
How much clay have you dug?
Sixteen good lumps! The kiln roars to life.
Honest, muddy work. The village builds on it.
mcaquests.quest.mason_lay_the_path.title: Lay the Path
mcaquests.quest.mason_lay_the_path.dialo: The market road is all mud. Lay 32 stone bricks and folk can keep their boots clean.
Straight and level, mind you. A crooked path shames us all.
How far has the path come?
Thirty-two bricks down — a fine, firm road.
The whole village walks easier for your work.
mcaquests.quest.mason_quarry_work.title: Quarry Work
mcaquests.quest.mason_quarry_work.dialog: The quarry's behind schedule. Break 48 stone and we'll catch up before the frost.
Swing steady. Stone doesn't forgive a lazy arm.
The blocks won't cut themselves, but as you wish.
Forty-eight blocks' worth — the masons will be pleased.
Strong back, that one. My thanks.
mcaquests.quest.mason_rebuild_the_wall.d: The wall's breached where the raiders came through, and a gap in the stone is an invitation. Set sixteen stone bricks along the breach and make it whole again.
Good. Lay them true — a crooked wall is half a wall.
Then the gap gapes, and we all sleep lighter for it.
How's the breach coming? Stone by stone, that's the way.
Solid masonry, flush and square. The wall holds again.
Honest work, honestly done. The village stands a little safer for your hands.
There's a wall that won't build itself. Twenty-four stone would set the next course nicely.
Good. A village is only as strong as its walls.
The wall waits. Stone is patient.
Two dozen blocks of good stone. Now we build.
When the wall stands, you'll know you helped raise it.
mcaquests.quest.mercenary_bounty.title: Bounty: Creepers
mcaquests.quest.mercenary_bounty.dialogu: There's a bounty on those hissing green cowards — they cratered a client's home. Bring me 5 dead creepers.
Watch the fuse and you'll be fine. Mostly. Go collect.
Bounty stays unclaimed. Pity — it pays well.
How's the bounty coming? Any booms?
Five creepers culled and not a scratch on the client's new wall. Nicely handled.
Bounty paid in full. You've got the makings of a fine mercenary.
mcaquests.quest.mercenary_contract_killi: I deal in coin for blood, and right now I'm overbooked. Clear 8 zombies off my contract and the pay's yours.
Smart. No questions, just results. I like that.
More for me, then. Your loss.
Contract's still open. How many left?
Eight bodies, contract closed. You work clean. I respect that.
Pleasure doing business. There's always more work for a pro.
mcaquests.quest.mercenary_pillager_bount: A pillager band's been shaking down travelers on the trade road. The crossbow crowd, the standard-bearers, all of them — clear out six and there's good coin waiting.
Watch for their crossbows. They shoot before they parley.
More for the next blade, then.
How many of the band have you put down?
Six raiders cold on the road. The merchants will breathe easier.
The road's safer for honest folk now. Take your bounty — you earned it.
mcaquests.quest.mercenary_witch_hunt.dia: A coven's been cooking trouble in the swamp — bad potions, worse luck. Find the crooked hut standing on stilts over the water; there's coin in it if you put down three of the witches.
Mind their throwing arm. Those bottles bite.
How many witches off the board? Try another swamp hut if that one's gone quiet.
Three covens' worth of mischief, ended. Here's your coin.
Clean work. I'll know who to call next time there's a contract.
mcaquests.quest.relations_a_meal_for_mot: My parent grows frail and forgets to eat. Would you carry six loaves of bread to them yourself, and see they take a proper meal?
Bless you. You'll find them near home, slow as they move these days.
I'll go myself when I can get away, then.
Have you reached my parent with that bread?
They ate? Truly ate? Oh, what a weight off me.
You fed my parent when I couldn't be there. That is no small kindness.
mcaquests.quest.relations_anniversary_gi: Do you know what day it is, my love? Our day. Bring home a cake and we'll mark another year together, just the two of us.
Oh, you remembered after all. I'll set out the good plates.
...Of course. Another year, another forgotten day.
Is the cake on its way, dearest?
A whole cake! You old romantic, you.
To another year, and many more. I'm the luckiest soul in the village.
mcaquests.quest.relations_child_treat.di: Pssst — can you keep a secret? I want cookies, but the grown-ups say no. Bring me six and I'll share!
Did you get the cookies yet?
Six whole cookies! You're the best!
mcaquests.quest.relations_childs_first_t: My little one's been so brave lately. I'd love to make them a soft toy lamb — could you bring three white wool to my child directly? Let them pick the softest.
They'll be over the moon. Look for them near the well.
Have you found my child with that wool?
Soft wool, straight into little hands — wonderful.
You should have seen their face. You've made a child very happy today.
mcaquests.quest.relations_cure_infected_: One of my kin has the rot in them — the zombie-sickness. A golden apple and a steady hand can still pull them back from it. Please, hurry, before they turn for good.
Go to them. The cure can't wait.
Then we can only pray, and bar the door.
Is my kin cured yet? Use the golden apple on them.
They're whole again? Thank every star above.
You gave my family their life back. We are forever in your debt.
mcaquests.quest.relations_cure_my_spouse: Something bit me in the dark, my love, and I can feel it taking hold — I'm so cold. There's a way back, a golden apple and a steady hand. Please. Don't let me turn.
Hurry, my heart. I'll hold on as long as I can.
No — don't go. Please don't leave me to this.
It's spreading... the cure, love, quickly.
The cold... it's loosening its grip. You're saving me.
I'm myself again. You pulled me back from the edge of something awful. I owe you my very soul.
mcaquests.quest.relations_escort_me_home: It's getting late and the road isn't safe alone. Keep close and keep the monsters off me, and I'll lead us back to the village before nightfall.
Stay near — I'll set the pace.
Then I'll risk the road myself, I suppose.
Keep moving with me, friend — we haven't long before dusk.
Home at last, and before dark! I knew I could trust you.
Safe and sound. I won't forget this kindness.
Night fell before we made it. We were lucky to survive — maybe next time.
mcaquests.quest.relations_escort_to_mark: I've goods to sell but the road to the next village runs through rough country. Keep me safe and I'll lead the way to the market town.
Wonderful. Stay close and let me pick the path.
Then my wares stay in the cart another week, I suppose.
The market's not far now — mind the road behind us.
Stalls and customers at last! We've arrived.
A safe road and a full market — couldn't ask for more. My thanks, friend.
mcaquests.quest.relations_family_reunion: The whole family's gathering under one roof for once, and I'll not have them go hungry. Carry eight good cuts of cooked beef to my kin — hand them over yourself — and we'll set a table to remember.
Wonderful! I'll start laying the places.
We'll make do with thin soup, then. Again.
Have you found them with the beef? They'll be sitting down by sundown.
Eight fine cuts — the table will groan with it!
Laughter and full plates under one roof. You gave us a night we'll always remember.
mcaquests.quest.relations_grandparents_b: The nights bite cold and these old bones feel every one. Would you bring your grandfather a proper bed to rest in? Wool and timber, that's all I ask.
You're a good grandchild. I'll make space by the window.
Ah, never mind an old soul's grumbling. Off you go.
Still drafty in here. Any luck with that bed?
A fine soft bed! I'll sleep like a babe tonight.
Warm at last, thanks to you. You've a kind heart, child of my child.
mcaquests.quest.relations_guard_village_: This is my village to protect, and the monsters grow bold. Help me thin them out — five of the undead should send a message.
Good. Watch the alleys and the dark corners.
How goes the cull? Five of them, remember.
Five down. The streets are quieter already.
The village owes you a debt. I'll not forget it.
mcaquests.quest.relations_heal_my_belove: I took a bad turn out there, my heart, and I'm hurting more than I'll admit. Press a golden carrot into my hand and stay with me till the ache fades?
Your touch already makes it better. Come here.
...It's fine. I'll mend on my own, as ever.
Still smarting, love. That golden carrot would help.
Oh, that's the stuff — the warmth is already spreading.
Right as rain, and all because you fussed over me. My darling healer.
mcaquests.quest.honored_envoy.title: An Honored Envoy
mcaquests.quest.honored_envoy.dialogue.o: You've become a friend to this village. Carry our banner well — bring 8 paper to seal the proclamation, and you'll be named among the honored.
mcaquests.quest.honored_envoy.dialogue.a: The scribes are waiting. Off you go.
mcaquests.quest.honored_envoy.dialogue.d: The honor will keep until you're ready.
mcaquests.quest.honored_envoy.dialogue.i: The proclamation still needs that paper.
mcaquests.quest.honored_envoy.dialogue.r: Paper at last. Let it be written.
mcaquests.quest.honored_envoy.dialogue.c: By the village's word, you are honored. Wear the name with pride.
mcaquests.quest.relations_lead_me_home.d: I've strayed too far and the light's failing. I know the way back — just keep close and keep the monsters off me, and I'll lead us home.
Stay near me. I'll set the pace.
Then I'll find my own way, and hope for the best.
This way — and don't let anything creep up behind us.
Home, and in one piece! I knew I could count on you.
Safe behind the walls at last. I won't forget this kindness.
We never made it... I was lucky to crawl away. Another time, perhaps.
mcaquests.quest.relations_letter_to_brot: My sibling lives here in the village, but we've quarreled and I'm too proud to go myself. Carry this letter to them — hold it in hand and give it over directly.
Thank you. They'll know my seal the moment they see it.
Perhaps I'll find another runner, then.
Have you found my sibling yet? They're never far from home.
They have the letter? Truly? Bless you.
Family is everything, in the end. My thanks — take this for your trouble.
mcaquests.quest.relations_light_the_beac: When the dark comes the little ones get frightened. Would you set out some lanterns around the village — six warm lights to say we're safe in here?
Bless you. A lit village is a brave village.
Then we'll huddle by the one candle, as always.
How many lanterns are glowing now?
Oh, it's lovely — like little stars come down to the fences.
The children stopped crying the moment the lights went up. You gave us a gentler night.
mcaquests.quest.relations_mend_the_quarr: My sibling and I parted on hard words, and pride keeps us both silent. Carry a single poppy to them for me — they'll know what it means.
Thank you. One flower can say what I can't.
Then the silence stretches on, I suppose.
Have you reached my sibling with the flower?
They took it? And didn't throw it back? That's a start.
We spoke tonight, first time in months. You mended what pride near broke. Thank you.
mcaquests.quest.relations_missing_child_: My child wandered off and hasn't come home. Please — search the wilds for any sign of them. Start with the forest where they liked to play.
Thank you. Bring word the moment you find anything.
Please... if you change your mind, I'll be here, waiting.
Any trace of my little one out there?
You found them? Out there, alive? Tell me everything.
Alive. Cold and frightened, but alive, and you were the one who found them. I will never be able to repay that.
mcaquests.quest.relations_protect_my_chi: My little one wants to gather flowers by the meadow, but I daren't let them go alone. Keep them safe for a couple of minutes while they pick?
Bless you. Don't let them out of your sight.
Then they'll have to stay inside today.
Are they still safe? Keep close to them.
Safe and sound, with an armful of flowers! Thank you.
You watched over my child as if they were your own. I won't forget that.
My child... no. I should never have let them out. Leave me.
mcaquests.quest.relations_repair_the_wel: The stonework around our well by the village center has crumbled. Lay eight stone bricks around it and it'll hold another lifetime.
Good. Build it sturdy — the whole village draws from that well.
How's the well coming along? Stone bricks, near the center.
Solid as bedrock now. Fine work.
The well will serve us for years thanks to you. The village thanks you.
mcaquests.quest.relations_reunite_with_s: Night caught me out and my heart's at home worrying. Guard me and I'll lead us to my beloved — I just want to be at their side before the dark deepens.
Thank you. Keep close and I'll find the way to them.
Then I'll hurry on alone and hope love is enough to keep me safe.
Almost to them now — don't let anything stop us.
There they are! Oh, thank you.
Reunited, and all because you walked the dark with me. Bless you.
We were parted by the dark... I made it, but only just. Another night.
mcaquests.quest.relations_search_the_rui: One of my kin went missing near the old mineshaft and no one's dared look. You're brave enough — search the tunnels and bring me any sign of them.
Thank you. Take a torch, and mind the drops.
Then they stay lost, and I stay haunted by it.
Have you reached the old tunnels yet?
You went down into the dark for us? Tell me what you found.
Down in all that dark, and you brought them back to the light. I had stopped letting myself hope. Thank you.
mcaquests.quest.relations_see_my_child_h: My little one wandered out and now it's dark. They can walk on their own legs — just guard them while they lead the way back to the village. Please, hurry.
Stay between them and the shadows. I'll keep a lamp in the window.
Please — don't leave them out there alone.
Are they safe? Are they close? I can't bear the waiting.
Is that— it's them! Home and whole!
You watched over my child as if they were your own. I will never forget it.
No... not my child. I can't speak of it. Leave me.
mcaquests.quest.relations_sick_villager_: *cough* ...I'm not well, friend. A golden apple would do me a world of good — could you spare one?
Bless you. I'll rest until you return.
A golden apple! Already I feel stronger.
The fever's breaking. You may have saved my life.
mcaquests.quest.relations_spouse_flowers: You always know how to make me smile. Would you bring me a handful of poppies, my love? Five would brighten the whole house.
You're too good to me. I'll be waiting.
I'll set these by the window. Thank you, my heart.
mcaquests.quest.relations_stranded_at_du: I wandered too far and now the sun's nearly gone. I can find the way myself if you'll keep the monsters off me — walk with me to the nearest village before something finds us.
Bless you. I'll lead — you just keep your blade between me and the dark.
Then I'll have to chance the road alone. Pray for me.
Stay close behind me — I daren't run.
Walls and torchlight at last! We made it.
I'd have died out there without you. I won't forget this.
They caught us on the road... I barely escaped. Leave me be a while.
mcaquests.quest.relations_sweetheart_coc: I've a terrible sweet tooth today, my heart. Would you bring me half a dozen cookies? I'll share — maybe.
You spoil me. I'll put the kettle on.
Hmph. I'll dream of cookies, then.
Six whole cookies! However did you know?
Mm. Saved you the last one — see how good I am to you?
mcaquests.quest.relations_teach_them_to_: My child keeps asking after the river. I haven't the time — but you might bring them four cooked cod and share a meal by the water? They'd treasure it.
They'll talk your ear off about minnows. Thank you for the patience.
Maybe when the days are longer. They'll understand.
Has my child had their fish supper yet?
Cooked cod, shared by the river — just what they wanted.
They came home grinning ear to ear, smelling of riverweed. You gave them a fine afternoon.
mcaquests.quest.relations_long_road_back: I'm farther from home than I've ever been, and I don't mind telling you I'm afraid. Guard me and I'll lead us back, however long the road.
Thank you. Keep your eyes on the treeline and I'll keep us moving.
Then I'm truly on my own out here. Heaven help me.
Still a long way yet. Don't let them flank us.
I never thought I'd see those walls again. We did it!
You brought me back from the far wilds. I owe you my life, plainly.
It was too far, too dark... I lost everything out there but my skin. Give me time.
mcaquests.quest.relations_trade_with_bla: Our blacksmith's been short of custom lately and it's wearing on them. Go strike a couple of trades at the forge — it'd lift their spirits and the village's.
Good of you. Two trades ought to do it.
Ah well. Coin's tight all round.
Been to see the blacksmith yet?
Heard the hammer ringing again — that's your doing.
The smith's in good cheer now. The whole village feels it. My thanks.
mcaquests.quest.relations_walk_me_to_bed: These old bones don't like the dark anymore. Would you walk beside me to my own bed? I'll lead — just see that nothing troubles us on the way.
You're a comfort. Let's go slow and steady.
Ah well. I'll sit by the lamp a while longer.
My own door at last. What a relief.
Tucked in safe, and all thanks to you. Sleep well, friend.
Such a fright we had... I'll not venture out after dark again soon.
mcaquests.quest.relations_walk_the_walls: I can't sleep with that moaning beyond the fence. You've a strong arm — would you walk the walls tonight and put down four of the dead for us?
Bless you. I'll rest easier knowing you're out there.
Then I'll lie awake and listen, I suppose.
Still hear them out there. Four would set my mind at ease.
It's gone quiet beyond the fence. Thank you, truly.
A neighbor who stands the wall is a neighbor indeed. My thanks.
mcaquests.quest.relations_widow_memorial: My spouse is gone, and the grave looks so bare. Gather three poppies and take them to my kin — they should lay the flowers, not me. I don't think I could stand at that graveside twice.
Thank you. They always loved the red ones.
I understand. Grief is a heavy thing to share.
Three poppies, and into my kin's hands. That's all I ask.
Three poppies. They would have smiled to see them.
The grave looks loved now. Thank you — truly.
mcaquests.quest.shepherd_a_dyers_dozen.d: The weavers want black wool for a mourning shroud. Twelve bales, if you can dye or shear them.
Solemn work, but honest. Thank you.
The loom waits in silence, then.
Twelve bales, dark as a moonless night. The weavers will begin.
A kindness to a grieving family. Bless you.
mcaquests.quest.shepherd_spin_a_yarn.dia: Can't spin wool without a little string to start the spindle. Bring me 16 lengths?
Spiders are good for something after all. Mind their bite.
Sixteen good lengths! The wheel can turn again.
You've spun me out of a fix. Thank you.
mcaquests.quest.shepherd_warm_blankets.d: Winter's biting and the elders shiver. Weave me 6 carpets and I'll see them warmed.
Soft and thick, mind. Old bones feel the cold.
They'll huddle closer to the fire, I suppose.
Six warm carpets! No elder freezes on my watch — or yours.
You've warmed more than feet today. Thank you.
The flock's been stubborn at shearing time. Bring me 12 wool and I'll make it worth the trouble.
Mind the sheep — they bite when they're cross.
Suit yourself. The looms can wait.
Soft and clean — just what I needed. Let's settle up.
The whole village will be warmer for this.
mcaquests.quest.template_cartographer_su: My maps have a blank corner where the %s should be. Travel there and bring back what you see?
Mark the landmarks well. A map is only as honest as its surveyor.
The blank stays blank, then. Another day, perhaps.
Still bound for the %s? The ink is waiting.
You've stood in the %s — I can see it in your boots. The map is richer for it.
Splendid surveying. The guild will want a copy.
mcaquests.quest.template_farmer_crop_req: The market's hungry for %1$s. Could you bring me %2$s of them?
Bless you — leave them by the stall when you're back.
Ah well. The crates can wait another day.
Fair trade, friend. The stall will be the envy of the road.
mcaquests.quest.template_fisherman_catch: The smoker's cold and the nets are empty. Hook me %1$s %2$s and we'll call it square.
Cast where the water runs deep. Patience pulls the line.
Bah. The fish can keep their secrets a while longer.
%1$s %2$s, fresh off the hook! The smoker thanks you.
Now that's a haul worth bragging about. Here's your share.
The roads aren't safe — too many %1$s about. Cull %2$s of them and the village will rest easier.
Good. Keep your blade close and your wits closer.
Then we post a double watch tonight. Be careful out there.
How many %s have you put down?
The watch owes you a quiet night. Take this for your trouble.
mcaquests.quest.template_kin_errand.dial: Family looks after family, don't they? Carry %1$s %2$s to one of my kin for me — hand it to them yourself, with a kind word.
Bless you. They'll be so pleased someone thought of them.
Have you found my kin with the %s yet?
You've a place in this family's heart now. That's not a thing we give lightly.
mcaquests.quest.template_librarian_knowl: The archive runs short of %1$s. Bring me %2$s and I'll see the records kept.
Wonderful. Knowledge survives only as long as its keepers are stocked.
A pity. The unwritten page forgets so quickly.
Have you found %1$s %2$s for the archive?
%1$s %2$s — the shelves will breathe again. Thank you.
A scholar's gratitude is a lasting thing. This is yours.
mcaquests.quest.template_mercenary_bount: Got a contract with your name on it — %1$s %2$s need putting in the ground, and there's coin for whoever's got the stomach. You in?
Good. Bring me proof, or just come back breathing — either works.
Suit yourself. The bounty doesn't spoil.
%1$s %2$s down. Clean work — here's your due.
Reliable and deadly. I'll keep your name at the top of the list.
mcaquests.quest.toolsmith_a_proper_kit.d: A young miner's heading out green. Craft an iron pickaxe so he doesn't dig with his fingers.
Good iron, good haft. He'll thank you for it.
He'll learn the hard way, then.
A proper pickaxe! He'll mine for years with this.
You've set a lad on a good path today.
mcaquests.quest.toolsmith_deep_delve.dia: I need raw iron straight from the rock. Mine 5 iron ore and I'll handle the smelting.
Take a torch and watch for cave-ins.
The veins will keep, I suppose.
Five good ores! The furnace is already warm.
Honest work. Come back when your pick is sharp again.
mcaquests.quest.toolsmith_sharp_and_read: The woodcutter's axe finally gave out. Forge a new iron axe so the firewood keeps coming.
Good steel, true edge. He'll fell oaks like saplings.
A keen iron axe! The woodpile will never run low.
Solid work. The whole lane stays warm because of it.
mcaquests.quest.toolsmith_temper_in_batt: A tool's only as good as the hand that's tested it. Take one of mine to the field and put down four of the undead — I want to know it holds an edge under strain.
Use it hard. I'll want the honest truth when you're back.
Then it stays on the rack, untried. Pity.
How's it holding up out there? Four of them, mind.
Four down and the edge still true? Then my temper held.
Field-proven and battle-tested. That's worth more than any showroom shine. My thanks.
mcaquests.quest.toolsmith_tools_of_the_t: Folk break more tools than they buy. Bring me 5 iron ingots and I'll keep the village digging.
A sharp tool is a happy farmer. My thanks.
The picks will dull without it, but as you like.
Five good ingots. The grindstone calls.
Come by when your axe needs an edge.
mcaquests.quest.unemployed_a_splash_of_c: My windowsill is so drab. Could you pick me 8 wildflowers? Any colors will do.
Oh, how lovely of you! The meadows are full this time of year.
Ah well. Grey days suit me, I suppose.
Eight blooms! My window will be the cheeriest on the lane.
You've brightened more than the sill, friend.
mcaquests.quest.unemployed_apple_a_day.d: My old knees can't manage the orchard ladders anymore. Would you pick me 6 apples?
Bless you, dear. Sweet ones if you can find them.
These old bones will go without, then.
Six rosy apples! You've made an old soul very happy.
Come sit with me sometime. You're always welcome.
mcaquests.quest.unemployed_berry_picking: The children do love sweet berries, but the bushes scratch so. Could you pick a dozen for them?
Mind the thorns! The little ones will be over the moon.
No treats for the children today, I suppose.
Twelve plump berries! The children will cheer when they see these.
You've made a whole row of little ones smile. Thank you.
mcaquests.quest.unemployed_egg_hunt.dial: I'd love to bake a cake but I've nothing to bake with. Could you bring me 6 eggs from the coop?
Wonderful! It's been an age since I had a treat.
Any eggs for my little cake?
Six whole eggs! I can almost smell it baking already.
I'll save you the first slice, I promise!
I haven't found my trade yet, but I do get hungry. Could you spare me 6 bread?
Truly? That's kinder than most folk bother to be.
No matter. I'm used to going without.
Did you bring anything to eat?
Six whole loaves — I haven't seen so much bread in weeks!
I won't forget this. One day I'll repay you, I swear it.
mcaquests.quest.unemployed_kindling.dial: My fire's nearly out and I've no trade to buy wood. Could you gather me 16 sticks?
Oh, thank you! A warm hearth is all I ask for.
That's all right. I'll manage... somehow.
Found any sticks for my fire?
Sixteen sticks! I'll be warm tonight thanks to you.
You're a good soul. I won't forget this kindness.
I've no trade and no coin, but I've got neighbors I care about, and there's three of the dead shambling too near our doors. You've a strong arm — would you see them off?
Thank you kindly. I'll keep folk indoors till it's done.
Fair enough. Not everyone's a fighter.
Still a couple of them lurching about out there.
All three? You've a brave heart, friend.
I can't pay you what a lord would, but you've my thanks and a neighbor's loyalty. That's worth something.
mcaquests.quest.weaponsmith_bone_collect: Skeletons have been rattling around the old ruins. Put down 6 of them and the roads will be safer.
Aim for the ribs. Bring me back nothing but quiet.
Then keep your shield up out there.
How many skeletons are left clattering about?
Six down? The night is a little less dangerous for it.
Steel and nerve — you've both. Well earned.
mcaquests.quest.weaponsmith_creeper_cull: Creepers keep blowing craters in my walls. Cull 3 of the hissing things and bring me peace and quiet.
Strike fast and step back — you know how they end conversations.
Boom. That'll be the wall again. Sure you won't help?
How many creepers left out there?
Three fewer walking bombs. My masonry thanks you.
Quiet at last. Take this — you've earned every bit.
mcaquests.quest.weaponsmith_drowned_dept: The drowned hoard metal down in the dark water — and the odd trident, too. Send five of them back to the deep and salvage what they're hiding.
Mind their tridents. They throw harder than you'd think.
Then the river keeps its secrets a while longer.
How many drowned have you cleared from the shallows?
Five of the river-dead put to rest. Good diving.
Whatever you hauled up, you earned. The forge thanks you.
mcaquests.quest.weaponsmith_proving_the_: I've forged a new blade and a smith's word means nothing — it's the field that proves steel. Take it out and put down six of the undead, then tell me how it held.
Mind the edge. Report back honest, now.
Then it hangs untested on the rack. A pity.
How does the blade bite? Six of them, remember.
Six undead and the edge still keen? Then I forged true.
Proven steel and a proven arm. Keep the blade — you've earned it twice over.
mcaquests.quest.weaponsmith_temper_the_b: Good steel starts with good iron. Bring me 6 ingots and I'll forge the village a proper blade.
Folded and tempered, it'll hold an edge for years. My thanks.
Then the militia drills with sticks.
Have you the iron for the forge?
Six honest ingots. The hammer falls tonight.
The next sword off this anvil is half yours.
mcaquests.quest.weaponsmith_the_horde.di: I forged a fine blade but I'm no swordsman. Put down 8 zombies with it and tell me how it cuts.
Aim true and report back. For science, as it were.
Untested steel is just a heavy bar.
How does the blade handle the dead?
Eight down? Then the temper holds. Excellent data.
You've proven my craft. Take this, with my gratitude.
The raid is upon us! Cut down the attackers before they overrun the homes — six of them, and quickly!
Then to arms. Watch the gates.
Then we hold the line alone. Pray it's enough.
Keep at them! The village is counting on you.
The village still stands because of you. We won't forget it.
We lost too much before help came. The village will remember the cost.
mcaquests.situation.avenge_the_fallen.of: We buried one of our own today, taken by the monsters. Don't let it be for nothing — hunt down eight of the undead and make them pay.
Good. Let them fear the village again.
Then grief is all we have left.
How many have you put down? Eight, I said.
Eight of them. It won't bring them back, but it's something.
The village mourns easier knowing the monsters paid. Thank you.
The moment's passed. We grieve, and we move on.
mcaquests.situation.cure_the_infected.of: One of our own is turning — the zombie-sickness has them. A golden apple, used in time, can still save them. Please, before it's too late!
Hurry to them. Every moment counts.
Then we can only bar the doors and grieve.
Have you reached them? Use the golden apple before they turn.
You pulled them back from the dark. The whole village breathes easier.
We were too slow. The rot took them. May they rest.
mcaquests.situation.defend_the_gate.offe: They're testing the gate again tonight. Plant yourself at the wall with me and cut down eight of them before they break through — hold this ground.
Then hold the gate. Not one of them gets past.
Then I hold it alone, and pray the bar holds too.
Hold the line! How many at the gate have you dropped?
Eight down and the gate still ours. Well held, watcher.
The gate stood the night because you stood at it. The village owes you a quiet dawn.
They breached before we cleared them. A hard night — and a harder morning.
The stores are nearly bare and bellies are growling. Bring sixteen loaves of bread and we'll see the village through the lean days.
Thank you. Every loaf keeps a family fed.
Then we ration what little we have and pray for a harvest.
Any bread for the stores yet? Sixteen loaves.
The granary's filling again. You've done us a great kindness.
No one goes hungry tonight, thanks to you. The village won't forget it.
The hunger set in before the bread came. A hard season, this.
mcaquests.situation.find_missing_child.o: A Child Lost to the Wilds
A little one from our family wandered off and never came home. Search the forest where the children play — bring us any sign of them.
Bless you. Hurry — the woods are no place for a child at night.
Then we keep our own vigil, and hope.
Any trace out in the forest?
You searched the wood? Tell us what you found.
At least someone cared enough to look. The family is in your debt.
The trail's gone cold now. We may never know what became of them.
mcaquests.situation.night_watch.offer.di: The dark brings monsters to our walls. Stand watch with me tonight — clear five of the undead before dawn and the village sleeps safe.
Good. Keep your blade ready and your eyes open.
Then I'll watch alone, as ever.
Still some lurking in the dark. Five, before sunrise.
Dawn's near and the streets are clear. Well watched.
Another night the village wakes whole. My thanks, watcher.
Dawn came and the work was unfinished. Tomorrow night, then.
The horns are sounding — raiders are on the village! Hold the wall and cut down eight of the attackers before they put the homes to the torch!
To the wall, then! Break their charge!
Then bar your door and pray the gate holds.
They're still coming! Eight of the raiders down — that's what we need!
Their line's breaking — you've turned the tide!
The village still stands, and that's your doing. We won't forget who held the gate.
They got through despite us. We'll be a long time counting the cost.
mcaquests.project.muster_the_militia.arm: If this village is to defend itself, the recruits need steel and arrows. Donate iron and shafts and we'll see them armed.
Keep the iron and arrows coming — a militia's only as good as its kit.
mcaquests.project.muster_the_militia.dri: Now blood them. Help the recruits cut down the undead pressing our walls — sixteen kills will make soldiers of them.
Every kill is a lesson. Keep the recruits in the fight.
mcaquests.project.rebuild_the_walls.gath: The walls won't mend themselves. Donate stone brick and a few torches and we'll have the materials to close the breaches.
More stone, more light — the masons are ready when the supplies are.
mcaquests.project.rebuild_the_walls.rais: Now we build. Set the stone along the breaches — sixteen blocks and the wall stands whole again.
Lay them true and tight. A wall with gaps is no wall at all.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_pantry_run.dia: I have not eaten properly in days and the fields will not tend themselves. Bring me bread and I will put it straight in my pantry.
You are a kind soul. I will keep working while you go.
I will manage. I always do.
Any bread yet? My stomach is keeping count.
Bless you. That will see me through the week.
A full pantry and a full belly. Back to the fields with me.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_water_for_the_: My throat is like a dry well. If you can spare water, I will not forget it.
Then I will keep working thirsty.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_a_proper_night: I am dead on my feet. See that I actually rest tonight instead of working through it.
If I nod off standing up, wake me and send me to bed.
The work will not wait for sleep.
Not rested yet. Do not let me talk myself out of it.
I slept. Properly. I had forgotten what that felt like.
A clear head at last. Thank you for insisting.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_care_for_the_y: The little ones eat before I do, and today there is not enough. Help me feed them.
You have my thanks before you have even gone.
We will make do, as always.
Look at them. They will sleep well tonight.
A village that feeds its young has a future. Thank you.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_first_shift.di: I am new to this trade and clumsy with it. Stay while I work a proper shift.
Then let us see if I can hold a day's work.
Perhaps another day, when I am braver.
Still at it. Do not let me wander off.
A whole shift. My hands ache and I am proud of it.
I am no master, but I am no longer useless.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_master_of_the_: I am within reach of the top of my trade, and there is a stretch of it I would rather not do with nobody watching. Stay for that stretch.
It is not dramatic. It is just a lot of days in a row.
The work will still be here when you change your mind.
Not there yet. It does not go faster for being watched, but it goes easier.
There. Did you see it? That was the moment.
As far as this trade goes here, and you were there for it. Somebody should be, for something that takes that long.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_a_balanced_day: I work, then I work, then I work. Help me keep to my shifts for once.
Hold me to it. I am terrible at holding myself to it.
There is always more to do.
Am I keeping to it? Do not let me drift.
A day that went the way it was meant to. Rare, that.
I had forgotten a day could feel like that.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_founding_chara: This place has no character yet. Help us build something it can be known for.
Then let us give the village a name worth saying.
A village can drift for a long time before anyone notices.
We are still just houses and mud. Keep going.
People will know us for this. I can feel it.
We are somewhere now, not just somewhere on the way.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_growing_commun: We need more than shelter now. Raise something civic and the rest will follow.
Good. I will find the hands if you find the will.
We will stay as we are, then.
Not built yet. These things take time and timber.
Look at it standing there. That changes a place.
A village with somewhere to gather is a village that stays.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_healthy_workfo: Half the village is hungry or half-asleep. Put us right and keep us right a while.
It is not one meal that fixes this. It is keeping at it.
Better in places. Not everywhere yet.
Look around. Everyone is upright and fed.
A village that can work is a village that can grow.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_plan_the_field: Before a seed goes in I need to know where it goes. Stay while I walk the rows.
