Good. Planning is half the harvest.
Then I will guess, and we will eat what guessing gives us.
Still pacing it out. A field misplanned is a year lost.
Every row accounted for. Now it can grow.
A planned field feeds a village. A guessed one feeds nobody.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_full_granary.d: A granary with a floor showing is a village one bad season from trouble. Fill it.
Wheat, bread, anything that keeps. I will find room.
We will hope for a kind winter, then.
Still light in there. Keep it coming.
Full to the rafters. I can sleep on that.
Let the season do its worst. We are ready for it.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_the_long_harve: I have farmed here my whole life. Help me make this the year they remember.
Then we work until the light goes.
There will be other years. Fewer, but other ones.
Not the year they remember yet.
This one. This is the one they will remember.
Forty seasons of learning, and this was the best of them.
Nets do not mend themselves and I cannot fish with holes. Bring me string.
Twelve should see the worst of them closed.
Then I fish with holes and catch half as much.
Still full of holes over here.
Mended. She will hold a proper catch now.
A whole net and a whole day ahead of me.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_dockside_catch: A proper dock changes everything. Build us one and watch what I can land.
Deep water needs somewhere to tie up. Get me that and I will do the rest.
Then I will keep fishing off the rocks like a boy.
No dock yet. The good water is still out of reach.
There she is. Now we are a fishing village.
Ships tie up here now. That is a different sort of place.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_deep_water_day: The dock is deep enough now to work the far water properly. Come out with me for a couple of tides and let us find out what is down there.
Cod, salmon, whatever runs. And I want the shifts kept properly, not half-worked.
I will fish the shallows. I always do.
Not enough in the baskets yet, and not enough days behind us either.
Full baskets and the shifts kept. That is what deep water is worth.
Days of it, off our own deep dock. This village eats from the far water now, and that was not true a season ago.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_shears_and_she: The flock has nowhere to be penned. Raise them somewhere and I can keep them.
Somewhere safe from the dark, that is all I ask.
Then I will count them each morning and hope.
Still no pen. Still counting each morning.
Penned and safe. I slept through the night for once.
A shepherd with a pen is a shepherd who keeps his flock.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_fill_the_wool_: An empty wool shed is a shed. Fill it and it becomes a trade.
Every fleece counts. Bring what you can.
The shed will keep. It is good at that.
Packed to the beams. That is a winter of work.
Wool enough to clothe the whole village twice over.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_the_whole_floc: I want to be the shepherd this village talks about. Stay while I earn it.
It is not the flock that makes a shepherd. It is the years.
The sheep do not mind either way.
Still learning them, after all this time.
I know every one of them by the way she walks.
The best flock in the valley, and they know it.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_fuel_the_smoke: A cold smoker is a useless one. Bring me fuel and I will keep it lit.
Coal, charcoal, I am not fussy. Just keep it coming.
Then it stays cold and the meat stays raw.
Lit and drawing well. Smell that.
Smoke in the rafters and meat that keeps. That is a butcher at work.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_stock_the_smok: The smokehouse is up but bare. Stock it and this village eats all winter.
Meat that keeps is worth more than meat that does not.
We will eat fresh and go hungry later.
Hung from end to end. Let the cold come.
Nobody in this village goes hungry this winter.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_the_winter_cur: Curing meat properly takes a lifetime to learn. Help me spend some of it.
Salt, smoke and patience. Mostly patience.
The old way will do. It always has.
Not there yet. Curing cannot be hurried.
That is the finest cure I have managed.
They will come from other villages for this.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_leatherworkers: I have an order to fill and no hides to fill it with. Help me out.
Leather, as much as you can carry.
I will tell them it is late. Again.
Still short. The order will not fill itself.
That is the order filled, and on time for once.
A reputation for delivering is worth more than the coin.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_tanned_and_rea: Tanning is slow, foul work and I need a proper run of it done.
Stay upwind and I will not mind the company.
Nobody blames you for the smell.
Still at the vats. This takes what it takes.
Every hide through and every one good.
Foul work, fine leather. That is the trade.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_the_master_tan: Everyone here calls me the tanner and nobody has seen me work a full week at it. Stay for three proper shifts and keep me in hides while you are at it.
Three shifts, start to finish. And thirty-two hides, because I will get through them.
Then the name goes on meaning nothing in particular.
Still short of hides, or still short of days. Usually both.
Three full days at the frames and stock to spare. That is a working tannery.
Nobody in this village has any doubt what I do now. That is worth more to me than any title somebody could hand out.
mcaquests.project.townstead_raise_the_do: Deep water is out there and we have nowhere to tie up. Bring timber and we will change that.
More timber. A dock is mostly patience and planks.
Now we build. When it is registered as a dock, the village will feel different.
Still not a dock. Keep at it.
mcaquests.project.townstead_pastures_and: The flock wanders and the dark takes them. Fencing first, then everything else.
Still gaps in the fence. Still losses in the morning.
With a pen and a shed we need shepherds who know their trade.
The pens are up. The skill is still coming.
mcaquests.project.townstead_a_working_vi: A village works when its people have what they need to work. Start with tools.
Still hands without tools in them.
Now the slow part: people who are genuinely good at what they do.
Coming along. Skill is not something you can donate.
mcaquests.project.townstead_well_fed_tow: Feeding everyone once is easy. Feeding them steadily is the work. Stores first.
The stores are not deep enough yet.
Now hold it. A village that eats well for a day has not solved anything.
Holding, but not for long enough yet.
mcaquests.project.townstead_find_our_cha: We are a collection of houses. I would like us to be a place. Materials first.
Build what suits us and keep at it until the village has a character of its own.
Still becoming. These things settle slowly.
mcaquests.situation.townstead_hunger_cri: Half of us have not eaten in days. Whatever food you can spare, bring it now.
Quickly. People are starting to go down.
Then we ration what is left and hope.
Food. Actual food. You have no idea.
You fed a village today. That is not a small thing.
The hunger passed, but not without cost.
mcaquests.situation.townstead_dehydrated: The workers are parched and the well is not enough. Bring water, quickly.
Before someone drops in the field.
We will drink less and work slower, then.
Nobody went down today. Thanks to you.
mcaquests.situation.townstead_exhausted_: Nobody here has slept properly in a week. Help us before someone falls.
Beds, quiet, anything. We are past pride.
We will keep going until we cannot.
Still on our feet. Only just.
A village that sleeps is a village that works.
mcaquests.situation.townstead_collapsed_: Someone has collapsed where they stood. Get them fed and rested before it is worse.
Hurry. They are not waking on their own.
Then we carry them inside and pray.
Still down. Still breathing, at least.
They are sitting up. Colour is coming back.
You may have saved a life today.
mcaquests.situation.townstead_master_art: One of ours has reached a mastery worth marking. Help us do it properly.
Nothing extravagant. Just enough for a proper evening.
We will raise a cup regardless.
Not much of a celebration yet.
Now that is a table worth sitting at.
They will remember this evening longer than the mastery.
mcaquests.situation.townstead_community_: The village has taken on a character of its own. Help us mark what we have become.
A place that knows itself is worth celebrating.
Perhaps we are not that sort of village after all.
The celebration is still being put together.
Everyone is here. Everyone knows why.
We know what we are now. That matters more than it sounds.
mcaquests.situation.townstead_new_civic_: We have raised something the village did not have before. Now it needs stocking.
It will fill up eventually, I suppose.
Stocked and ready to be used.
Built and stocked. That is how a village grows.
mcaquests.title.keeper_of_seasons.descri: Saw one farmer through a whole year, and the village through the winter at the end of it.
mcaquests.title.harborhand.description: Built a harbour from wet stones to deep water, and lit the way back in.
mcaquests.title.trusted_hand.description: Stayed through every dull year of somebody else’s apprenticeship.
mcaquests.title.village_chronicler.descr: Gave a nameless settlement a character, and kept its people well while it grew into one.
mcaquests.title.roadwarden.description: Reopened the road between two villages and walked a neighbour down it in one piece.
mcaquests.title.mender_of_kin.descriptio: Turned a cure into an expedition, and stayed until the voice came back.
mcaquests.title.bellwarden.description: Prepared a village for a raid nobody could promise would come, and stood in it when it did.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_spring_in_the_: The ground has gone soft enough to work and I have not half the seed I need. Stay with me through the sowing and I will not forget it.
Then we start at first light. Bring what seed you can find.
The furrows will wait. Not long, but they will wait.
Seed in the ground and a day's work still ahead of me.
That is the field sown. Come and look at it before the rain does.
Every furrow is planted. Come back when the summer heat sets in — that is when this field will really need you.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_heat_over_the_: The sun has not let up in days and I cannot stop to drink and keep the crop alive both. Bring me something to see the afternoon out.
You are kinder than the weather. I will take it.
I will manage. I usually do.
Still parched, and the rows still need walking.
That is better. I can feel the difference in my hands.
The crop came through the heat and so did I. Find me at the harvest, when the whole autumn is riding on one week of work.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_harvest_under_: It is all ready at once, the way it always is, and I have one pair of hands. Everything we get in this week is what we eat until spring.
Then we work while the light holds.
Some of it will rot in the field. That is how it goes.
More still standing out there than lying in the store.
The store is full. I have not seen it like this in years.
Nothing was left in the field. When the first frost comes, come and see whether this village eats well on it.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_winter_at_the_: A full store is not the same as a fed village. I want to see everyone come through this winter — not just my own household.
Then we count it by who is standing in spring.
The store is there. Whether it reaches everyone is another matter.
Some are keeping well. Not enough of them yet.
Walk the village and look at them. That is what a good year looks like.
A whole year, and the fields carried every one of us through it. This place knows what it grows now.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_harbor_first_p: I have been landing my catch on wet stones since I got here. Give this village a dock and I will show you what the water is really worth.
Drive the first piling and the rest follows.
No dock on that shore yet.
There it stands. I can tie up to something at last.
A registered dock, on our own water. Come back and work a tide with me — a dock nobody uses is just wood.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_harbor_working: The dock is up, and now it has to earn itself. Fish the tide with me and let the village see what comes off it.
Cod on the ebb, salmon on the flood. Off we go.
The tide turns whether we are on it or not.
Not enough in the baskets to call it a day's work.
Both baskets full and the shifts behind us. Good water.
That is what the dock was for. It gets dark out there early, though — come back and we will do something about the lights.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_harbor_lantern: Our dock has outgrown its lights. Half the winter I am tying up in the dark, and one slip on those boards is all it takes.
Lanterns along the rail and chain where the boards give.
I will go on feeling my way, then.
Still stretches of that dock a person could walk off in the dark.
You can see the whole run of it from the water now.
Lit end to end. The boats coming in late can find us. One thing left: this harbour is still too shallow for the deep-water boats.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_harbor_deep_wa: Take the harbour as deep as it will go. If we can berth a real boat here, this stops being a village with a jetty and becomes a port.
Deep water, and everyone comes home off it.
We will stay a jetty a while longer.
Not deep enough yet, and the village still smells of fields, not salt.
Deep water at our own dock. Listen to how they talk about this place now.
From wet stones to a harbour with a name. Whatever else this village becomes, it will always have been built facing the sea.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_pasture_first_: I lose lambs to the treeline every season because there is nothing between them and it. Give me a pen and that stops.
Posts first, then rails. It does not need to be pretty.
Then I keep counting them twice a night.
Nothing registered out there yet. The flock is still loose.
A proper pen. I slept through last night for the first time in a while.
Fenced and registered. Now there is somewhere safe for lambs to be born — come back when they are.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_pasture_lambin: A pen with six sheep in it is a hobby. Help me build a flock worth shearing, and bring shears — mine have been sharpened past saving.
Keep them near the pen. They wander if you let them.
Flock is growing, but not by enough yet.
Look at them all. And proper shears at last.
A flock, in a pen, with something to cut the wool. It will all be sitting in the rain, mind — we need a roof over it before the wet season.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_pasture_wool_u: Wet wool is worth nothing and I have been stacking it under a tarpaulin. Build us a shed and I will fill it.
Four walls and a dry floor. That is all it takes.
Shed or wool — I am still short of one of them.
Dry, stacked, and out of the weather. That is a season's work stored properly.
Wool under a roof and a flock that keeps growing. There is only so far a shepherd gets on instinct — the rest is years. Come and put in the years with me.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_pasture_keeper: Stay with me long enough and I will know this flock the way I know my own hands. That is not a thing you can rush.
Then we take it season by season.
I will get there. Slower, is all.
Still learning them. Every flock is different.
I can tell you which of them is off her feed from across the field.
Pens, wool, and a shepherd who has earned the word. This is a village that keeps animals well, and people can tell.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_smokehouse_fir: I have been butchering on a stump behind my house. It is not fit work and everyone knows it. Build me a proper place.
Somewhere with a floor I can wash down. Please.
No workplace registered yet. Still the stump.
Four walls and a fire. I could weep.
A registered butcher's, with a first fire lit in it. It only becomes a trade when it runs to a schedule — come and work one with me.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_smokehouse_hon: A smokehouse eats charcoal faster than anyone expects. Keep me stocked and stay for a couple of shifts — I want the village used to seeing it running.
Charcoal in the corner and the doors open on time.
I will run it cold half the week, then.
Fire is hungry and the shifts are not done.
Stocked and running to time. That is a working smokehouse.
Two shifts kept and fuel in the corner. Come back before the cold — a smokehouse is really for winter, and winter is what I am worried about.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_smokehouse_win: Smoked meat is how this village gets to spring. Fill the racks, and then walk the streets with me and see whether it reached anybody.
Beef, pork and mutton. Nobody is fussy in winter.
We will find out the hard way how far it goes.
Racks half empty and the cold coming on.
Full racks, and people who look like they have eaten.
The whole village is provisioned. There is one thing left that I want, and it is not for the village — it is for me.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_smokehouse_leg: I want to be good at this. Not adequate — good, the way the old butcher three villages over is good. Stay with me while I get there.
Then you will be here a while.
Adequate keeps people fed. I suppose.
Getting there. Slowly, the way it should be.
I know what I am doing now. It took long enough.
The smokehouse will outlast me, and somebody will learn it here after I am gone. That is what I wanted out of all this.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_apprentice_too: I have decided to take this seriously. I need three things to start: something to keep the hours by, something to write in, and a meal I do not have to think about.
A clock, a book and bread. Not much to start a life with.
Another year of doing it by guess, then.
Still short of what I need to begin properly.
That is everything. I can make a start with this.
Time, notes and a full stomach. Now come and see what a full day of it actually looks like.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_apprentice_fir: Anyone can work an hour. Stay with me for two proper shifts, start to finish, and I will know whether I have this in me.
Start to finish. No slipping off at midday.
I will try it alone. It is harder alone.
One good shift is not two.
Two full days, both of them mine. I did not think I would manage it.
Two shifts kept end to end. The next part is longer and duller and matters more — that is where most people stop.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_apprentice_tru: There is a stretch in every trade where nothing feels like progress and you have to do it anyway. I would rather not do that stretch on my own.
Then stay for the dull part. That is the real favour.
It is a long stretch alone.
Grinding away. It does add up, apparently.
People have started asking me things instead of telling me.
Nobody watches me work any more. There is one thing left after that, and it is the part I have wanted since I was small.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_apprentice_mas: Four more shifts and the last of the ground I have left to cover. Then I stop being someone who is learning this.
I will finish it eventually. Everyone does.
Close. Closer than I have ever been.
It is done. I have nothing left to be shown.
You stayed through the whole of it — the tools, the shifts, the dull years. Whatever I make from here, some of it is yours.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_character_firs: Travellers ask what sort of place this is and I have no answer. We are not known for anything yet. Help me change that.
Build something we would be recognised by. Anything, so long as it is ours.
Then we stay the village on the way to somewhere else.
Still nothing here that anyone would name us for.
There. That is the beginning of a character.
We have a first mark on the map. Now we have to find out which one of our traits is really us — come back when the village has settled on it.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_character_choo: We have started to lean one way. I want to be sure it holds before I write it down anywhere — stay a while and let us see if it sticks.
Give it time. Character is not decided in an afternoon.
It may settle without being watched.
It has held. That is what we are.
Written down and no longer in doubt. A name is easy to lose, though — it wants building on.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_character_stre: A name that rests on two buildings is a rumour. Build until nobody could mistake us for anywhere else.
More of the same, and better. That is how it works.
Nobody argues about what this village is any more.
Our character is built into the streets now, not just spoken about. What is left is whether the people in them are well.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_character_livi: A village can be famous and miserable. I would rather we were known for something and the people here were well while we were known for it.
Both at once, then. It is more work.
We can be one without the other. It happens all the time.
One of the two is lagging. Usually the people.
Look at the place and look at the people in it. Both.
This village has a name, a character and a population that is doing well under it. That is worth writing down properly, and I intend to.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_breakfast_befo: I am due at work shortly and I have not eaten since yesterday. I will not last the morning like this.
Bread would do. Bread would do very well.
I will work through it. People do.
Still hollow, and the bells are not waiting.
That is the first thing I have eaten in a day. I can feel it working.
I will get through today on that. It is a small thing to you and it was not a small thing to me.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_day_off_means_: A Day Off Means a Day Off
My schedule says rest and I have been finding work to do all the same. Sit with me and stop me going back to it.
If I stand up, tell me to sit down.
There is always something that needs doing.
I feel human again. That took less time than I expected.
A whole rest day, actually rested. I will be better at everything tomorrow for it, which is the part I always forget.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_lanterns_for_l: My shift runs into the dark and I am working by feel out there. A few lanterns would change the whole night.
Hang them where I actually stand, not where it looks nice.
I know the place well enough in the dark. Mostly.
I can see what my hands are doing. That is new.
Lit, and I stayed on schedule right through the dark stretch. It is a different job with light on it.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_water_bearers_: Half this village has not had a proper drink today and nobody has noticed but me. Walk the rounds with me before somebody goes down.
Every house. We do not skip the ones who never complain.
I will do the rounds alone. It will take twice as long.
Too many still parched out there.
Go and look at them. That is what a village looks like when somebody checked.
Nobody went down today. That is not nothing — it very nearly went the other way.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_rest_after_the: I have been up since the alarm and I am past the point of being any use. I do not want to be alone while I go down for a bit.
Stay close. That is all I am asking.
I will keep standing. It is what I am for.
I slept because somebody was watching. I would not have, otherwise.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_a_week_kept_we: One good day is luck. Give me a whole week of them — worked properly, fed properly, slept properly — and I will believe I can live like that.
Five shifts. And do not let me skip the meals.
I will keep having the good days by accident.
Some days kept. Not the week.
Five shifts, and I am in better shape at the end than the start.
A whole week held together. I know what it takes now, which means I can do it again without you.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_infirmary_befo: Every winter somebody is treated on a kitchen table because we have nowhere better. I would like that to be the last time it happens.
A roof, a bed, and something to treat them with.
The kitchen table has served so far.
No infirmary yet, and the mornings are already cold.
A room set aside for the sick, and stocked. Before the frost, even.
Whoever falls ill this winter has somewhere to go. That is what an infirmary is — a decision made in advance.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_rooms_for_the_: Travellers pass through and keep going, because there is nowhere here to stop. Build us an inn and they will stay long enough to spend something.
Beds and a light in the window. That is the whole trick.
They will keep going. They always do.
Nowhere to sleep here yet but somebody’s floor.
Rooms made up and lit. It looks like somewhere you would stop.
Somewhere to stop. Small thing to build, and it changes what this village is on a map.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_bookkeepers_ce: Nobody has counted this village in years and I do not trust the last figure. Bring me paper and speak to a few people while you are at it.
Paper first. Then a farmer, a guard and a cleric — they know who is missing.
The old figure will have to stand.
Half a census is worse than none.
Every column filled in. I know exactly who lives here now.
The register is current for the first time in years. Ask me anything about this village and I can answer it from the page.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_lanterns_for_t: Once a year we light the graves, and once a year something comes up out of them while we do. I would rather not do both alone.
Candles first. Keep the sword handy.
The graves will go dark this year, then.
Still dark out there, and still not quiet.
Every stone lit and nothing left standing that should not be.
They are remembered properly and they are resting properly. Both matter, and only one of them is about the dead.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_a_real_worksho: I have an anvil in the open air and a fire I have to relight every morning. Give me a forge with walls and I will show you what I can actually do.
Walls, an anvil, and something that holds heat.
The open air has done for years.
Still working out of the weather’s way rather than in a workshop.
Anvil under a roof and two furnaces holding their heat. Finally.
A registered smithy. Everything I make from now on will be better than everything I made before it, and that is entirely down to the roof.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_first_workday_: They have put me on the roster for the first time and I do not want to turn up empty-handed. Something to keep the hours by, and something to write in.
Show me where I am meant to stand, too. I have never actually looked.
I will work it out on the day. Everyone does.
Not ready yet. I would rather be ready.
Compass, book, and I know exactly where I am going in the morning.
A full shift, start to finish, and nobody had to fetch me. I am glad somebody was there for the first one.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_the_elders_old: I have walked the same round of this village for forty years and I would like to walk it once more with somebody who will listen on the way.
The workshop first. Then home. That was always the order.
I know the way. I have always known the way.
Still walking. There is no hurry in it.
Home, by the road I have always taken. Thank you for the company.
You now know this village the way I know it — which streets flood, which door sticks. Somebody had to be told before I stopped walking it.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_names_in_the_f: There is a relative of mine in this village whose half of our family record I have never seen. Take them a book and hear what they remember.
Write down whatever they say. Even the parts that contradict mine.
Half a record is what most families have.
You have not spoken to them yet.
You have both halves. Come and put them side by side.
Two accounts of the same family, and they disagree in three places. That is not a problem — that is what a family is.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_spring_bells_a: Spring has come round again and this village looks exactly as grey as it did in February. Let us do something about that before anyone notices I care.
Flowers where people walk. And a bell, so it is official.
Still greyer than a spring has any right to be.
Colour on every path and a bell to ring over it.
People slowed down on their way to work this morning. That was the whole point of it.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_stores_against: Every year somebody says we have enough put by and every year we are counting coal in February. Let us over-provision for once.
Coal, bread and something with meat in it. In that order of importance.
We will count coal in February again, then.
Not enough put by. It never looks like enough in autumn.
That is more than we need, which is exactly the right amount.
Nobody will be rationing this year. I would like to be wrong about needing all of it, and I usually am not.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_commission_sal: People know us for the water now, and the dock still goes dark at dusk. Bring in a season's catch and put some light on the boards while you are there.
Cod first. The lanterns can wait until your hands are cold.
The tide does not need us to be interested.
Full baskets and a lit dock. That is a fishing village.
Anyone coming in off the water tonight will see us before they smell us. That is worth more than the catch.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_commission_bre: We are a farming place and the pen looks like an afterthought. Grow the flock and stack the feed where people can see it.
Lambs and hay. It should look like plenty, because it is.
It will look like an afterthought a while longer.
Full pen, hay to the rafters. Somebody will ask what our secret is.
Travellers stop at the fence now instead of walking past it. That is the whole point of doing it properly.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_commission_wat: We have a reputation for holding ground and I intend to keep it. There is a band of them working the treeline. Deal with it, and light the approach.
Clear them first. Light second. Both before dark.
Still some of them out there, and still too dark to see them coming.
Cleared and lit. Nobody is walking up on us tonight.
That is why they leave us alone. Not because we are lucky.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_commission_ink: We are known for keeping records and our reading room has one lectern and no blank books. That is a joke I would rather stop hearing.
Books, paper, and somewhere to put them down.
Still more readers than there is anything to read.
Two lecterns and a shelf of blanks. Somebody can actually work here.
People come here to write things down now. In a hundred years that will be the only reason anyone knows we existed.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_commission_iro: This is a working village and my forge is running at half what it could. Give me the furnaces and the stock and listen to the difference.
Anvil, furnaces, iron. In that order.
Both furnaces lit and stock to hand. Now it sounds like a smithy.
You can hear this place working from the treeline. That is what we are known for and now it is true.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_commission_mar: Trade is what we are known for and half the stalls have not seen a customer in days. Go round every one of them and bring the takings back.
Buy something from everyone. It matters more than what you buy.
Everyone has taken something today, and here is the till to prove it.
A market only works when people believe it is worth turning up to. You just made everyone believe it for another season.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_commission_wel: People come a long way to see this place and the inn is dark by the time most of them arrive. Light it and make up the rooms.
Lights outside, beds inside. Nothing complicated.
They will arrive in the dark and think we are shut.
You can see it from the ridge now. Warm, from a long way off.
Nobody arrives here at night and wonders whether they should have come. That is the entire job.
mcaquests.quest.townstead_commission_bel: This village is known for its dead and I would rather we were known for remembering them well than for what walks when we do not.
A candle for every name. And keep your back to the wall.
The names will go unlit again.
Names still in the dark, and something still moving between them.
Every stone has a light on it and the ground is quiet.
They are remembered and they are at rest. People find this village unsettling — they should know it is also kind.
mcaquests.quest.road_the_missing_mile.di: There is another village out that way and no living soul here has walked to it. Go and find it, and speak to whoever keeps their maps.
Take the ridge line. It is longer and it is survivable.
The blank part of the map stays blank.
You have not reached them yet, or you have not spoken to them.
You found it. Come and tell me what is between here and there.
Two villages, one road, and now somebody has walked it. It is not safe yet — come back and we will do something about what lives on it.
mcaquests.quest.road_clear_the_cut.title: Clear the Cut
mcaquests.quest.road_clear_the_cut.dialo: Nobody will use a road they can be robbed on. There is a cut near the far end where they wait. Make it not worth waiting there.
Go loud. The point is that they tell each other.
Then it stays a road nobody uses.
Still not a road I would send anyone down.
The cut is clear. It will not stay clear on its own.
Safe enough to walk, for now. What it needs next is somewhere to stop halfway — a road without a resting place is still a gamble.
mcaquests.quest.road_raise_the_waystatio: Build something at the far end that a traveller can reach before dark: gravel underfoot, light overhead, a fire and somewhere to leave what they cannot carry.
It does not need to be grand. It needs to be there.
They will keep sleeping in ditches.
Half a waystation is a pile of gravel.
Gravel, lanterns, a fire and a chest. It is a place now.
There is somewhere to stop on that road. All that is left is to prove it works — and that means walking somebody down it who is not you.
mcaquests.quest.road_caravan_through.dia: I am going to walk it myself. If the road is what we say it is, I will get there. If it is not, I would rather find out with you beside me.
Set the pace. I will keep up or I will say so.
I will go alone one of these days and you will hear about it.
Still walking, and still a long way from their gate.
Their gate. I have never stood at another village's gate before.
The road is open, and I am the proof. Somebody will make that walk every week now, and none of them will know how it got there.
I am not well and I know what it is. Take word to the cleric before I stop being able to ask — and bring back whatever they say.
Spider eye, bottles, and something to write the list on — all of it into the cleric's hands, not mine.
Then somebody will find me like this and it will be a shock to them.
Have you seen them yet? I am asking you every hour, I know.
You have the list. Read it to me — I want to know how bad it is.
Nether wart, they said. Of course it is. You are going to have to go somewhere very unpleasant for me.
mcaquests.quest.remedy_embers_and_wart.d: It only grows in the one place, and the things that guard it burn. I am sorry to ask. I am more sorry that I cannot go.
Six should be enough. Bring seven if you can.
I understand. I would think twice too.
Still down there? I keep listening for the portal.
You came back. That is honestly the part I was worried about.
Wart and blaze rods. Everything after this happens on our own hearth, which is a relief to both of us.
The last of it is gold, and two things that have no business being in the same room as gold. The cleric was very clear about the quantities.
An apple, an eye and a measure of powder. Do not improvise.
I will keep. For a while.
Still short. And I am worse than I was yesterday.
That is all of it. Everything the list said.
It is made. Whatever happens tomorrow, somebody tried everything, and I would like that written down.
mcaquests.quest.remedy_the_returning_voi: Do it now, and then stay. The cleric said the first hour after is the one that decides it, and I do not want to spend it alone.
Stay close. If I say something strange, ignore it.
Then I stay like this, and you both know what that ends as.
Still turning. Do not go far.
I know your name again. I did not, an hour ago.
I remember all of it — the wart, the waiting, you not leaving. Most people would have handed over an apple and walked away.
mcaquests.quest.bell_shields_for_neighbo: If something comes at this village tonight, four people have weapons and nobody has a shield. I would like to fix the easy half of that.
The shields and the bows come to me — three shields, two bows — and I will put them in the right hands myself. Shields to the ones who will stand. Bows to the ones who will not.
We will find out the hard way what we are short of.
Still not enough to arm the people who would turn out. Bring them to me as you make them, one at a time if that is how they come; I count each one in.
That will do for the people who would actually come.
Everyone who would fight has something to fight behind. The next problem is that we cannot see what is coming.
mcaquests.quest.bell_the_lantern_line.di: Everything that has ever gone wrong here came out of a dark field. Light the approaches and put something in the way while you are at it.
Light first. A wall is only useful if you can see over it.
Still gaps a person could walk through unseen.
Lit and walled. I can see the treeline from the square.
We can see them coming now. Which means the next thing is to be awake when they do — come back at nightfall.
mcaquests.quest.bell_watch_before_dawn.d: Stand the watch with me tonight. Not patrol — stand it, all the way through, and deal with whatever walks up.
No sleeping until it is finished. That is the whole exercise.
I will stand it alone. I have before.
Still dark, and still things out there.
That is the last of them and the sky is going grey.
A night held, start to finish. If a real raid comes, we know what we can do. I hope it never does. It will.
mcaquests.quest.bell_when_the_horns_answ: This one has no deadline, because I cannot promise you a raid. When one comes — and one will — be here, and stay standing next to me until it is over.
Nothing to do until it happens. Keep your gear where you can find it.
Then it will happen and we will manage without you.
Nothing yet. That is not the same as nothing coming.
It is over. Look at the square and tell me it was not worth preparing for.
Shields, lights, walls, a night of practice, and then the real thing — and we are all still here. That is not luck. That was the year we spent on it.
mcaquests.quest.relic_beneath_the_well.d: There are ruins under the sand out east with pottery in them older than this village. Bring me two pieces and make something whole out of them.
Brush, do not dig. The sherds break if you are rough with them.
They have waited this long. They will wait longer.
Sherds are no good on their own. Two, and then the pot.
A whole pot, with somebody else's story pressed into the sides of it.
Somebody made this and then everything they knew disappeared. It is on my shelf now, which is the closest thing to being remembered.
mcaquests.quest.atlas_of_four_horizons.d: I want one atlas that covers every kind of country there is: forest, mountain, ocean and the red badlands. Walk all four and come back to me.
Take your time. An atlas made in a hurry is a drawing.
Then it stays four separate maps.
Not all four yet. I will know if you guess one.
All four horizons. Sit down and tell me about them in order.
One atlas, four countries, one person who walked all of it. Nobody else here will ever need to make that journey.
mcaquests.quest.drowned_ledger.title: The Drowned Ledger
There is a ruin on the seabed that used to be somebody's town. I want to know what is left of it, and the things living in it will object. The lanterns it still burns are where the crystals come from.
Crystals for the record. Drowned because they will not let you take them.
It has been down there a long time. It can stay down there.
Still down there? Come up if your air is short — and break the sea lanterns for the crystals, not the drowned.
Crystals and a clear seabed. What did it look like?
Somebody lived there, and now we know roughly who and roughly when. It stops being a hazard on the chart and starts being a place.
mcaquests.quest.echoes_below.title: Echoes Below
mcaquests.quest.echoes_below.dialogue.of: There is a city under the stone that nobody built and nobody left. I want a compass that points home from inside it — and I want you to come back.
mcaquests.quest.echoes_below.dialogue.ac: Quietly. Everything about that place rewards being quiet.
mcaquests.quest.echoes_below.dialogue.de: Sensible. Most people say no to this one.
mcaquests.quest.echoes_below.dialogue.in: Still down there. I am not going to pretend I am not counting the days.
mcaquests.quest.echoes_below.dialogue.re: You are out. Sit down before you tell me anything.
mcaquests.quest.echoes_below.dialogue.co: A compass that finds the way back from the worst place there is. I hope nobody ever needs it. I am glad it exists.
mcaquests.quest.nether_relay.title: The Nether Relay
mcaquests.quest.nether_relay.dialogue.of: Everything I brew that is worth brewing needs blaze rods, and there is exactly one place to get them. Six of them, into my hands. I will make it worth the burns.
mcaquests.quest.nether_relay.dialogue.ac: Six rods. Eight of them, to get six. They come to me — Deliver in my Quests menu, or Gift them to me one by one. I will count each rod as it arrives.
mcaquests.quest.nether_relay.dialogue.de: I will brew the dull things, then.
mcaquests.quest.nether_relay.dialogue.in: Not enough rods to fire the stand. Bring me what you have rather than carrying them about — Deliver in my Quests menu, or Gift them to me. The count keeps.
mcaquests.quest.nether_relay.dialogue.re: Rods. I can work properly for a month on this.
mcaquests.quest.nether_relay.dialogue.co: Every useful thing on my shelf for the next month starts with what you carried out of there.
mcaquests.quest.trial_by_fire.title: Trial by Fire
mcaquests.quest.trial_by_fire.dialogue.o: I will not sell a blade to somebody who has not been anywhere. Go somewhere that would kill you, make the blade yourself, and bring back the rods.
mcaquests.quest.trial_by_fire.dialogue.a: Diamond. If you come back with iron I will know you turned around.
mcaquests.quest.trial_by_fire.dialogue.d: Come back when you have been somewhere.
mcaquests.quest.trial_by_fire.dialogue.i: Not finished. I can tell without asking.
mcaquests.quest.trial_by_fire.dialogue.r: Diamond, and rods to prove where it was made. Good.
mcaquests.quest.trial_by_fire.dialogue.c: Now I will sell you a blade, because now you know what one is for. Most people never find out and buy one anyway.
mcaquests.quest.long_way_home.title: The Long Way Home
mcaquests.quest.long_way_home.dialogue.o: I have family in the next village along and I have never once made the walk. I would like to. I would not like to do it alone.
mcaquests.quest.long_way_home.dialogue.a: Whatever pace you set. I will not slow you down deliberately.
mcaquests.quest.long_way_home.dialogue.d: Perhaps next year. I say that every year.
mcaquests.quest.long_way_home.dialogue.i: Still walking. It is further than people say.
mcaquests.quest.long_way_home.dialogue.r: There it is. I did not think I would see it.
mcaquests.quest.long_way_home.dialogue.c: I walked to another village. At my age. I am going to tell everybody, and they are going to be bored of it by winter.
mcaquests.quest.honey_for_the_healer.dia: Honey is half of what I use on burns and I am down to the last jar. Find the bees, help them along, and bring me back a proper stock.
Gently. An angry hive gives nothing and costs a lot.
I will ration it. Somebody will be unlucky.
Still short, and burns do not wait for a good harvest.
Bottles and blocks both. That is months of work covered.
The next person who comes in with a scalded arm will be seen to properly. That is what a stock of honey actually is.
mcaquests.quest.last_banner_home.title: Bring the Last Banner Home
mcaquests.quest.last_banner_home.dialogu: A band of them took a banner off us in the spring and I have wanted it back every day since. Take it off whoever is carrying it now, and bring me two of their crossbows while you are at it.
The ones in the iron coats will be guarding it. Expect them. The two crossbows come to me — Deliver in my Quests menu, or hold one out and choose Gift. Either counts, and one at a time is fine.
It is only cloth. It is not only cloth.

Not enough of them dealt with yet. Look to the mansion in the roofed forest, or wait for the horns of a raid. When you have a crossbow, bring it to me — Deliver in my Quests menu, or Gift it to me. I keep the tally.
That is the band broken, and the crossbows are ours now.
They will send another band eventually. This one will not be back, and I have my banner.
mcaquests.quest.horse_for_the_courier.di: I carry messages on foot and it takes me two days each way. Tame me something with four legs and then show me the road it will be running.
Near the village, so I can look after it. Then the far end of the route.
Two days each way it is.
Either no horse or no road walked. Both, please.
A horse and a route. I can be there and back before dark now.
This village hears news the same week it happens now. That is a bigger change than it sounds like.
mcaquests.quest.feast_of_many_tables.dia: Nobody eats together here any more. Take bread to the farmer, meat to the butcher and something sweet to the cleric, and let us see who turns up.
Three different people. It does not work if you give it all to one.
We will keep eating at our own tables, then.
Not everyone has been asked yet.
All three have something to bring. That is a feast.
Everyone stayed until dark. They have not done that in years, and it took nothing but somebody deciding to ask.
mcaquests.quest.monument_of_names.title: A Monument of Names
mcaquests.quest.monument_of_names.dialog: We bury people and then we forget where. I want something in the middle of this village with every name on it, and a light kept on them.
Stone, because it has to last. Candles, because somebody has to tend it. And a written book of the names, given to me when it is filled.
We will keep forgetting. It is easier.
Half a monument is a building site. The book of names comes to me when you have written it.
It is up, and lit, and the book is ready for the names.
Every name we have is on it and there is room for the ones we do not have yet. That is the part I could not do without you.
mcaquests.project.townstead_four_seasons: We are going to fill one larder for the whole year rather than scrape through four times. It starts with seed, because everything does.
Seed and roots. The dull end of a year's food.
Summer is when we eat well and forget we will not always. Put some of it aside while there is some to put aside.
Bread, honey and something with meat in it.
Everything comes in at once and most of it will spoil if it stays where it grew. Get it into the larder.
The larder is filling. Keep it coming while the weather holds.
A full larder proves nothing on its own. What I want to see is the village still on its feet with the larder half empty.
Watching the village rather than the shelves now.
mcaquests.project.townstead_harbor_quart: A harbour is mostly other people's timber. Bring what you can spare and I will turn it into somewhere boats can tie up.
Planks, logs, chain and light. In roughly that order of urgency.
Now it has to become a dock somebody could work off, and the water has to start meaning something to this village.
A dock is up. Whether the village is a harbour yet is another question.
Deep water, and a village that would be described as a port by somebody who had never been told to say so.
Deeper, and more of us make our living off it every month.
mcaquests.project.townstead_civic_quarte: I want a quarter of this village that belongs to all of it: somewhere to be treated, somewhere to be recorded. That starts as a pile of stone.
Stone, glass, books and something to keep the sick going.

An infirmary and a bookkeeper. Between them they cover being ill and being remembered, which is most of what a village needs from its centre. A library, a cartographer, a music store or a graveyard all count toward the same reputation for learning, if you would rather build one of those.
One of the two is standing. The other is still a plan.
Now make it the thing we are known for. Five buildings that all point the same way and nobody will describe us as anything else.
Getting there. It takes more buildings than people expect.
mcaquests.project.townstead_apprentices_: Nobody here learns a trade properly because nobody can afford the year it takes. Fund that year and we will have people who actually know things.
Books, clocks, iron and food. An apprenticeship is mostly food.
Three people who are past being watched while they work. That is the difference between a village that survives and one that runs.
Some of them are getting there. Trades take the time they take.
One person at the top of their trade, and the places for them to teach it. That is a guild rather than a habit.
Close. It is always the last stretch that takes the longest.
mcaquests.project.townstead_rest_for_all: Half this village sleeps badly and works tired and nobody has thought of it as a problem you could solve. Beds and a decent supper is the whole plan.
Beds, bread and something to drink. It is not complicated.
Now let it work. I want to walk through this place and not pass a single person who is running on nothing.
Better than it was. Not yet what I asked for.
mcaquests.project.townstead_known_far_an: Travellers decide what a village is in the first five minutes. Let us make those five minutes worth having.
Beds, lights, something sweet, and maps so they can find us again.
An inn, and enough of a reputation for hospitality that somebody mentions us unprompted three villages away.
Somewhere to hear something, and enough conversation in the square that it sounds like a place rather than a stopping point.
The square is louder than it was. That is the measure.
mcaquests.project.roads_and_lanterns.roa: Every path out of this village turns to mud in autumn and goes dark at dusk. Both of those are fixable and neither of them ever gets fixed.
Gravel, stone and light. Unglamorous and overdue.
mcaquests.project.roads_and_lanterns.lig: Now lay it. Every stretch you surface is a stretch nobody twists an ankle on walking home.
Laid as far as it goes. Keep going.
mcaquests.project.roads_and_lanterns.roa: Tell people it is done. A road nobody knows about is a road nobody uses.
Word is getting round. Slowly, the way word does.
mcaquests.project.walls_before_winter.st: We have been lucky for three winters and I do not intend to rely on a fourth. Stone, iron and light, and we will not need the luck.
Piling up. It always looks like too much until you start building.
mcaquests.project.walls_before_winter.ra: Put it up where it matters, not where it is easy. The gaps are the whole point of a wall.
Rising. Mind the low ground on the north side.
mcaquests.project.walls_before_winter.pr: A wall is a promise until something tests it. Stand behind it and let something test it.
Holding. That is what we built it for.
mcaquests.situation.townstead_first_fros: There was ice on the trough this morning. Whatever we have not put by is what we do not have, and I have just counted.
Bread, coal and meat, and then we see how everyone is holding up.
We will find out in February whether that was the right call.
Colder every night and the shelves are not full.
Stocked, and people look like they have eaten. Both at once.
We will get through this one. I did not think that a week ago.
The frost settled in with the shelves half empty. People are rationing and nobody is talking about it, which is how it always goes.
mcaquests.situation.townstead_spring_pla: The ground turned overnight and the whole year rides on the next fortnight. Seed, roots, and somebody working the field properly.
Every day we lose now is a week we lose in autumn.
We will plant late. We always survive planting late.
Ground open and not enough in it.
Sown, and a full shift behind it. That is a spring done right.
Everything that will feed us this year is in the ground on time. That has not happened in a while.
Planting ran late. It will be a thin autumn, and it will not be anybody's fault in particular.
mcaquests.situation.townstead_coming_of_: They are grown, as of this week, and nobody has given them anything to be grown with. A way to keep time and a way to keep a record would do it.
And walk with them to wherever they are meant to be. Once.
They will work it out. Everyone works it out.
They are still standing about waiting to be told what happens now.
Look at them. Somebody made a fuss and it mattered.
They will remember that somebody marked the day. That is the entire point of marking days.
The week passed and nobody said anything. They are getting on with it, which is not the same as it having gone well.
mcaquests.situation.townstead_retirement: They worked their last full shift this week and told nobody. I am not letting that pass without a cake and somebody walking them home.
Something sweet, something hot, and your arm on the way back.
They would say they preferred it quiet. They would be lying.
Nothing on the table yet and they are pretending not to notice.
A proper table, and they are still here at it.
Forty years of shifts and somebody finally said thank you out loud. They are not finished — they are just finished with the roster.
Their last shift went by like any other. They will not bring it up and neither will anyone else.
mcaquests.situation.townstead_broken_rou: Half this village is somewhere it should not be at this hour and none of them can tell me why. Start with one person and work outwards.
Get one of them back on their own schedule. The rest tends to follow.
It will sort itself out. It usually does. Usually.
Still drifting. Nobody is where the day says they should be.
Back on the hour, and looking better for it.
The whole village is where it should be and nobody remembers the week it was not. That is what fixing something quietly looks like.
The routine never came back on its own. People are eating at odd hours and sleeping worse, and it will take a season to settle.
mcaquests.situation.townstead_new_harbor: The dock reached its second stage overnight and it is not finished until it is lit and moored. And somebody should land a catch off it first.
Lanterns, chain, and then go and use the thing.
It will get finished eventually. Everything does.
Half rigged and nobody has fished off it yet.
Lit, moored, and a full basket landed on the boards.
First catch off the new dock. Somebody will tell that story for years and get most of it wrong.
The dock stands unlit and unused. It will still be there when somebody gets round to it.
mcaquests.situation.townstead_crossroads: This village stopped being one thing this week and became two at once. That is worth a festival, and a festival is cake and light and people talking.
Cake, bread, lanterns. And go and actually talk to people.
We will let it pass unremarked, like we do.
Not much of a festival yet.
Lit, fed, and the square has not been this loud in years.
Two kinds of village, one square, and everybody in it. Whatever we become next, this is the night people will date it from.
Nobody marked the change. The village is two things now and it happened without a word said about it.
mcaquests.situation.caravan_stranded_at_: Somebody is a long way outside the border and it went dark an hour ago. They are not coming back on their own.
Get to them, then get them home. Slowly is fine.
They will be out there all night, then.
Inside the border and still walking. Stay with them a while yet.
Home, and nothing worse than cold. A night outside the wall is not a small thing to survive.
Nobody went out after them. They found their own way back eventually, and they have not said much since.
mcaquests.situation.monster_in_the_cella: There is something under my floor and it has been there since the light went. I am not going down there and I am not sleeping either.
Whatever is down there, deal with it. I will wait up here.
I will sit up with a torch, then. Again.
It has gone quiet. Stay a minute, in case quiet is not the same as empty.
Empty, and I can hear the house settling instead. I will sleep tonight.
Whatever it was moved on by itself. The floor is quiet and nobody has been down to look.
mcaquests.situation.lost_survey_party.of: The Survey Party Did Not Return
They went out to map the ruins eight days ago and the rest of the party came back without them. Somebody has to go and look properly.
Start at the ruins. That is where they were headed and nobody checked.
No word. I am not going to pretend that gets easier.
You found them. Bring them to me before you tell me anything.
Eight days out there and they walked back in. Most of these stories do not end this way and I know it.
The search wound down the way searches do — not with a decision, just with fewer people going out each morning.

mcaquests.quest.iceandfire_fire_dragon_h: A fire dragon has taken the ridge east of us, and the smoke reaches the fields. Kill it, and the village breathes again.
Then go while the wind still favours you. Watch the sky, not the ground.
A wise refusal. Braver folk than you have burned for less.
The dragon still lives. I can smell it from here.
You brought the ridge back to us. Come, tell it properly.
One fire dragon fewer in the world. The fields will grow again.
mcaquests.quest.iceandfire_ice_dragon_hu: An ice dragon has settled north of the pass, and nothing thaws where it sleeps. End it before winter comes early.
Take a warm cloak and a steady hand. Its breath is worse than its teeth.
Stay by the fire, then. Someone else will go.
The frost has not lifted, so the dragon has not fallen.
The north is quiet again. Sit, and tell me how.
An ice dragon down. The pass will be open by spring.
mcaquests.quest.iceandfire_lightning_dra: A lightning dragon rides the storms over the moor, and it has taken three herds already. Bring it down.
Good. Strike between the thunder, not with it.
Then we wait for it to come to us. I had hoped for better.
The storms still circle. Your work is not done.
The sky is empty. You have earned every word of this.
The moor is quiet, and the herds can graze. That was well done.
mcaquests.quest.iceandfire_hydra_hunt.di: There is a hydra in the marsh, and every hunter I send comes back with fewer arrows and more stories. Kill it.
Bring fire. Steel alone only makes more of it.
Sensible. I would not go either, and I forged the blade.
The marsh still hisses at night, so the hydra still lives.
You did it. I want to hear about every head.
The marsh is only a marsh again. Take this, and my thanks.
mcaquests.quest.iceandfire_dread_purge.d: The dread walk again from the old graveyard, and they do not tire as we do. Cut down six of them, whatever kind they are.
Then go tonight. They are thickest before dawn.
I do not blame you. I have seen what they leave behind.
They are still coming. Six is not many, but it is six.
The road is walkable again. Come inside.
Six fewer, and the gate can stay open past dusk. Well fought.
mcaquests.quest.iceandfire_dragon_seeker: This seeker points at dragons, or so the trader swore. Take it out past the treeline and use it once, so we know whether he lied.
Hold it up where the sky is open. That is all it asks of you.
Fair. It may well point straight into a fire dragon's mouth.
You have not used it yet. It cannot lie until you do.
So it does work. Sit down and tell me where it pointed.
Then the trader was honest for once. That is worth knowing.
mcaquests.quest.iceandfire_netherite_dra: A rider came through asking for netherite dragon barding, all four pieces. I cannot make it, but you can find it.
Head, neck, body and tail. Anything less is worse than nothing.
Then the rider waits. She has waited a season already.
Not the whole set yet. A dragon in half a suit is a dragon in none.
All four. Lay them out and let me look at the work.
The rider will pay in stories for a year. Here is my share of it.
mcaquests.quest.iceandfire_netherite_hip: Hippogryph armor in netherite is the only kind that survives a fall. Find me a set and I will fit it myself.
One set, whole. Bent plates are for the scrap pile.
Then the bird flies bare, and I will not watch.
Still no armor. The bird is still bare.
That is the piece. Give it here before you change your mind.
Fitted and buckled. That bird will outlive us both now.

mcaquests.quest.bountiful_board_discover: Work gets posted on the board now, out where anyone can read it. Go and look at what people are asking for.
Good. Read the whole thing, not just the top notice.
Then you will keep hearing about the work secondhand, and late.
The board is still there. It does not read itself.
You found it, then. What did they want?
Now you know where to look. That is half of getting paid.
mcaquests.quest.bountiful_contractor.dia: Anyone can read a notice. Take two of them down and finish them, then come back and tell me about it.
The notices will still be up when you change your mind.
Still short. Turn them in at the board, not to me.
Both of them? Then you have been busy.
Two contracts closed. People will start asking for you by name.
mcaquests.quest.bountiful_specialist.dia: There is one on the board nobody has touched in a week. Take the hard one and finish it.
The hard one. Not the one beside it.
It will still be there, going yellow, waiting for somebody braver.
The difficult notice is still pinned up. That tells me everything.
You took it down? Then say so plainly, I want to hear it.
The one nobody would take. That is a reputation, that is.

mcaquests.quest.capitals_royal_escort.di: The sovereign rode out to the border stones this morning and will not take an escort of ten. Take them home yourself, and stay close.
Close, I said. Not behind them at a polite distance.
Then I will walk it myself and hope the road is kind.
They are still out there. The road does not get shorter while we talk.
Home, and whole. The hall can breathe again.
The herald will put your name to it. That is worth more here than coin.
mcaquests.quest.capitals_petition_to_the: Half the village has a complaint and none of them can write. I have put eight of them on paper — take the lot to the Hand.
The Hand, mind. Not the sovereign. Go over the Hand's head once and you never get in again.
Then the complaints stay in my drawer, going stale.
Still carrying them? Paper does not improve with age.
All eight delivered? Good. Somebody in that hall will actually read them.
That is eight households who will stop shouting at me. Take this.
mcaquests.quest.capitals_the_accolade.di: You walked the sovereign home. Now clear the pillagers off our roads and bring a good iron sword to the throne — that is how a knighting is asked for here.
Twelve of them, and a blade fit to be seen. The sword comes back to you; it is the showing that counts.
There is no shame in it. Not everyone wants a title hung on them.
The roads are not clear yet, and the hall has not seen your steel.
Kneel when the sovereign speaks, and do not thank them until they have finished.
Rise, then. The chronicle will carry your name with a rank in front of it.
The heir insists on walking the village without a guard. I cannot forbid it. You can stand near them for an hour and nobody will call it an insult.
Stay within sight. An hour, no wandering off to sell things.
Then I will lose sleep over it, as usual.
The hour is not up, and you are not near them.
An hour, and not a scratch. That is how it is supposed to go.
Nothing happened, and that is the whole point. Here.
mcaquests.quest.capitals_coronation_gift: A new reign should start with something gold in the hall. I cannot spare the ore — find a gilded helm and put it in the sovereign's hands yourself.
Gold, and clean. A dented one says the wrong thing entirely.
Then the hall stays bare and people will talk about that instead.
No gold, no gift. The court notices these things.
Present it properly. Both hands, and say nothing clever.
The herald cried it out before you were through the door. Well done.
mcaquests.quest.capitals_the_chroniclers: The herald has filled the last book and is writing on the backs of tax rolls. Take them something they can actually write in.
A book with empty pages. Not one already full of somebody's poems.
Then this year goes unwritten, and next year nobody remembers it.
The herald is still writing on tax rolls. It is undignified.
Hand it over yourself. They like to know who to thank in the margin.
The chronicle keeps going. That is not nothing, in a place like this.
mcaquests.quest.capitals_envoy_of_the_al: We are sworn allies now, which means letters. Four sheets to the ambassador, and do not read them on the way.
Four. Folded as they are. The ambassador counts.
Alliances go quiet when nobody carries the post.
The ambassador is still waiting, and ambassadors remember waiting.
Delivered, then. The alliance holds another season.
Two courts stayed friendly because you walked. Take it.
mcaquests.quest.capitals_a_lords_due.dia: You are sworn to this capital, so I will be plain: twenty-four emeralds buys me a lordship, and I have twenty-three years of good service and none of the stones.
Twenty-four in the end. Bring them in handfuls if you must — I will hold what you bring — but do not come to me at twenty with a story.
Then I stay what I am, which is what everyone expected.
Still short. What you have already given me is counted and kept; bring the rest and I will go and stand in front of the throne.
All of it? Then I will go and stand in front of the throne today.
They said the word and it stuck. I will not forget who paid for it.
mcaquests.situation.capitals_the_empty_t: The throne is empty and the hall is full of claims. Write down twelve of them and get them to the Hand before somebody settles this with steel.
Twelve claims, on paper, to the Hand. Quickly.
Then it gets settled the other way, and I will be here to see it.
The hall is still shouting. The Hand still has nothing in writing.
The Hand has them all. Somebody can be chosen now.
A succession, argued instead of fought. You will not get a statue for it, but you should.
Too late. They stopped writing and started shouting names.
mcaquests.situation.capitals_drums_of_wa: War was declared this morning and the first thing that comes is not soldiers, it is the scum who follow armies. Hold the village.
Ten of them off the fields, and four of the axemen. Do not let them reach the houses.
Then get inside and bar your door with the rest.
They are still in the fields. I can hear them from here.
The fields are quiet. Come in off the wall.
The war goes on somewhere else now. That is the best any of us gets.
They got through. We will be burying people for a week.
